papers.title: Early--Narrow and Late--Wide Populations of GRB X-ray Flares
papers.result: A rest-frame GMM of $(t_{\rm pk},w)$ yields two populations: early–narrow (~80%, $\langle t_{\rm pk}\rangle\simeq10^{2}\,{\rm s}$, $w/t_{\rm pk}\lesssim1$; center $\log_{10}(t_{\rm pk},w)=(1.97,1.85)$) and late–wide (~20%, $\langle t_{\rm pk}\rangle\simeq10^{3.5}\,{\rm s}$, $w/t_{\rm pk}\gtrsim2$; center $(3.49,3.80)$). Their mean energies are consistent, $\langle\log_{10}(E_{\rm iso,f,rest})\rangle=51.13\pm0.10$ versus $50.66\pm0.20$ (K–S $p=0.22$). Early–narrow flares follow $L_{\rm avg,f,rest}\propto t_{\rm pk,rest}^{-1.74^{+0.24}_{-0.24}}$, while late–wide flares give $-0.19^{+1.01}_{-0.93}$; the combined slope is $-1.60^{+0.12}_{-0.12}$, shallower than $L_{\rm pk}\propto t_{\rm pk}^{-3}$. The global fit $\log w_{\rm rest}=\alpha+\beta\log t_{\rm pk,rest}$ has $\beta=1.21^{+0.06}_{-0.06}$, but only early–narrow flares are significant ($\beta=1.04^{+0.12}_{-0.13}$, $w/t_{\rm pk}\sim0.76$ versus $\sim2.04$). Waiting times are $\sim76\,{\rm s}$ versus $\sim2950\,{\rm s}$.
papers.problem: The origin of GRB X-ray flares is unresolved: they may be prolonged central-engine activity or external-shock variability, and it is unclear whether one temporal scaling describes all flares.
papers.method: Light curves from 100 redshift-known Swift-BAT GRBs (89 fitted; 61 with flares) are modeled with asymmetric Norris profiles. Rest-frame $t_{\rm pk}$, $w$, asymmetry, and $E_{\rm iso,f}$ adopt flat $\Lambda$CDM with $\Omega_{\rm m}=0.286$ and $H_0=70\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$. A multivariate GMM classifies $(t_{\rm pk},w)$; K–S, Spearman, and Bayesian regression test relations. Luminosity is $L_{\rm avg,f,rest}=E_{\rm iso,f,rest}/w_{\rm rest}$, and accretion timing is compared with $t_{\rm visc}\sim\alpha^{-1}(H/R)^{-2}\Omega_K^{-1}$.
papers.reason: This Swift-XRT population study separates early–narrow and late–wide GRB X-ray flares and tests prolonged accretion against external-shock variability, directly constraining compact-object central engines and relativistic outflows.

papers.title: New Constraints on the Ultrahigh Energy Neutrino Flux from the First Array-Wide Search with the Askaryan Radio Array
papers.result: The array-wide diffuse search observes $n=0$ events against an expected background of $0.13\pm 0.01$ (stat.) $^{+0.05}_{-0.06}$ (syst.). The Feldman–Cousins $90\%$ CL limit is the strongest among techniques over $50$–$1000\,\mathrm{EeV}$. Analysis-level expectations are $\mu=5.3$ (Global UL; $2.6\sigma$, $99\%$ exclusion), $\mu=2.4$ (Muzio; $1.3\sigma$, $90\%$ exclusion), $\mu=1.6$ (KM3NeT; $0.8\sigma$, $77\%$), $\mu=0.4$ (Kotera; $27\%$), and $\mu=0.2$ for both $100\%$ protons and Fang pulsars ($<1\%$). Low-energy systematics are $\sim 50\%$ (Askaryan model) and high-energy systematics $\sim 150\%$ (neutrino–nucleon cross section).
papers.method: ARA stations A1–A5 plus the A5 phased array are analyzed from January 2013 through December 2023, corresponding to $28$ station-years ($25.9$ after quality cuts; $10.6$ array-equivalent years). Each string uses $150$–$850\,\mathrm{MHz}$ antennas with station triggers kept at $\le 5$ events/s and the phased array at $\le 11$ events/s. Sensitivity for $50$ configurations is computed with NuLeptonSim and AraSim for an $E^{-1}$ spectrum. Cuts were set on a random $10\%$ sample with the remaining $90\%$ blinded; surface and thermal cuts retain $56\%$ and $85\%$ of simulated $E^{-1}$ neutrinos, and the benchmark-flux efficiency is $28\%$. Models are tested with $p=\mathrm{Poiss}(n=0\mid\mu)$ and Feldman–Cousins $90\%$ CL limits.
papers.reason: This first array-wide ARA diffuse search is directly relevant to ultrahigh-energy neutrino and UHECR-source studies: zero events set the leading flux limit at $50$–$1000\,\mathrm{EeV}$ and exclude some trans-GZK proton source models.

papers.title: Spectral Constraints on Line-Seed Inverse-Compton Models for the MeV Feature in GRB 221009A
papers.result: No line-seed inverse-Compton candidate is shown to satisfy photon supply, relative components, LAT consistency, and escape together. In the observer-directed Thomson limit, $\epsilon^{\rm IC}_{\rm obs}\simeq 2\gamma_e^2\epsilon(1-\beta_e\mu_i)/(1+z)$, while a head-on collision approaches $4\gamma_e^2\epsilon/(1+z)$. For host-frame $Ly\alpha\simeq 10.2\,{\rm eV}$ and $H\alpha\simeq 1.89\,{\rm eV}$, scattering to $10\,{\rm MeV}$ needs $\gamma_{e,Ly\alpha}\simeq 531$ and $\gamma_{e,H\alpha}\simeq 1.23\times 10^3$. A log-normal electron distribution seeded by H$_2$ $2.122\,\mu{\rm m}$ ($0.584\,{\rm eV}$) matches two published intervals at $E_{\rm c,H_2}=11.5$ and $8.8\,{\rm MeV}$, with $\gamma_0=3.30\times 10^3$ and $2.69\times 10^3$ and $s_\gamma=0.087$ and $0.177$; the corresponding trial UV centroids are about $210$ and $161\,{\rm MeV}$ with standard deviations about $35$ and $55\,{\rm MeV}$. None of 40 molecular combinations lies below the adopted central envelope at all sampled energies, and trace minima are about $3.46$, $1.48$, $1.60$, and $1.40$. Even under ideal excitation and internal escape, compact reference-line densities fall short by factors of approximately $4$–$9$; precursor-assisted deficits remain at least about $4.3$, or about $87$–$1.7\times 10^2$ for single photon use. A decreasing centroid does not uniquely imply electron deceleration, and the four-interval calibration $\gamma_0\simeq(3.30,2.70,1.62,2.08)\times 10^3$ is non-monotonic.
papers.problem: Can H$_2$ ultraviolet-fluorescence photons, hydrogen recombination lines, or metal K-shell lines, scattered once by relativistic electrons, explain the Fermi-GBM MeV feature of GRB 221009A without violating the simultaneous LAT spectrum, local photon supply, timing, angular geometry, and the adopted spectral envelope?
papers.method: The model uses anisotropic single-scattering kinematics and a Klein–Nishina emissivity. With recoil parameter $b\equiv 4\gamma_e\epsilon/(m_ec^2)$, the local response is $d\ln\epsilon^{\rm IC}_{\rm obs}/d\ln\epsilon=1/(1+b)$. The flux is $F_{\epsilon_{\rm obs}}(\epsilon_{\rm obs},t_{\rm obs})=\frac{1+z}{d_L^2}\int d^3\boldsymbol{r}\,j_{\rm IC}[(1+z)\epsilon_{\rm obs},\Omega_{\rm s},\boldsymbol{r},t_{\rm ret}]e^{-\tau_{\rm esc}}$, integrated on equal-arrival-time surfaces with $dt_{\rm obs}=(1+z)(1-\beta_e\mu_{\rm s})dt$. Electrons follow $\frac{dN_e}{d\ln\gamma_e}=\frac{N_e}{\sqrt{2\pi}s_\gamma}\exp\left[-\frac{(\ln\gamma_e-\ln\gamma_0)^2}{2s_\gamma^2}\right]$; $\gamma_0$ and $s_\gamma$ are calibrated to photon moments, and 40 PDR-template plus external-screen combinations are compared with reconstructed central spectra. Optically thin component ratios scale as $\frac{F_{2,B_2}}{F_{1,B_1}}=\frac{u_2}{u_1}\frac{\mathcal{P}_{2,B_2}}{\mathcal{P}_{1,B_1}}$.
papers.reason: This paper quantitatively tests whether atomic and molecular line photons, inverse-Compton scattered in a relativistic outflow, can produce the evolving MeV feature of GRB 221009A, a direct constraint on jet radiation and dense circumstellar or molecular seed supply.

papers.title: Detectability of Seyfert galaxies in point-source and stacking searches with a global network of neutrino telescopes
papers.result: In all three scenarios the Circinus Galaxy is by far the brightest southern Seyfert in both neutrinos and MeV $\gamma$-rays. If Seyferts supply the diffuse astrophysical neutrino flux up to ${\sim}100\,\mathrm{TeV}$ and Circinus has at least the population-average neutrino luminosity, the IceCube--Baikal-GVD--KM3NeT/ARCA--P-ONE network reaches $5\sigma$ on Circinus by 2038 at the latest; Appendix C gives ${\sim}6.1\sigma$ (NGC 1068-like, $5\sigma$ in 2033) and ${\sim}6.2\sigma$ (average, $5\sigma$ in 2038) by 2040. The scenarios are $(P_{\mathrm{CR}}/P_{\mathrm{th}},\eta)=(0.5,56)$ (NGC 1068-like), $(0.01,1)$ (average), and $(0.5,1)$ (optimistic), with $\eta=B^{2}/\delta B^{2}$. Using NGC 1068 parameters for every source exceeds the TeV diffuse flux by $3.8\sigma$; fitting the flux below ${\sim}100\,\mathrm{TeV}$ instead requires $P_{\mathrm{CR}}/P_{\mathrm{th}}\lesssim 0.05$ and $\eta\lesssim 10$ for most sources. Other nearby Seyferts remain hard to detect individually. For $F_X\ge 10^{-11}\,\mathrm{erg}\,\mathrm{cm}^{-2}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$, the 2040 optimal stack is $N_{\mathrm{src}}\sim 50$--$70$ with Circinus and ${\sim}100$--$130$ without it.
papers.problem: Can X-ray-bright Seyfert coronae be discovered as individual neutrino point sources, or only by X-ray-informed stacking, if a hidden coronal origin like NGC 1068 accounts for the diffuse astrophysical neutrino flux without accompanying TeV $\gamma$-rays?
papers.method: Protons are stochastically accelerated in a magnetized corona of size $R_c=r_c R_S$ with $R_S=2GM_{\mathrm{BH}}/c^{2}$, and neutrinos come from photohadronic interactions on coronal X-rays plus hadronuclear interactions; $\gamma$-rays are $\gamma\gamma$-absorbed and emerge mainly at MeV energies. Forecasts use PLE$\nu$M and Asimov data in bins of $\log\hat{E}$ and $\Delta\Psi^{2}=|\hat{\Omega}-\Omega_{\mathrm{src}}|^{2}$, with $\lambda_{ij}(\boldsymbol{\theta})=\lambda_{ij}^{\mathrm{astro}}+\lambda_{ij}^{\mathrm{atm}}$ and $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{tot}}=\prod_k\mathcal{L}_k$. Each of IceCube, Baikal-GVD, KM3NeT/ARCA, and P-ONE is assigned $1\,\mathrm{km}^{3}$; water detectors are given IceCube-like effective area but better angular resolution for $E_{\nu}\gtrsim 10\,\mathrm{TeV}$ because of the longer Cherenkov-photon scattering length.
papers.reason: The paper quantifies neutrino point-source and stacking detectability of X-ray-bright Seyfert coronae with a global telescope network, which is relevant to compact-object neutrino observations but is not central to FRB, supernova-engine, or jet-breakout work.

papers.title: Identification of the C IV $λλ$5801, 5812 Emission in the Off-Nuclear TDE 2025abcr
papers.result: VLT spectra identify optical C IV $\lambda\lambda 5801,5812$ (C IV $\lambda 5805$) in off-nuclear TDE 2025abcr, at a projected offset of $9.3\,\mathrm{kpc}$ and $z\simeq 0.05$. The proposed excitation is continuum fluorescence plus photon trapping in the $312\,\mathrm{\AA}$ transition, analogous to WN winds and requiring strong EUV irradiation and high optical depth. A single-temperature fit gives $T_{\mathrm{BB}}\simeq 2\times 10^{4}\,\mathrm{K}$, below $3\times 10^{4}\,\mathrm{K}$ from the UV plus blue optical; the lack of rapid variability implies a reprocessing photosphere with $R\sim 10^{14}\,\mathrm{cm}$. Broad-line widths are relatively narrow, $\sim 2500$–$3000\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$, while He II and N III FWHM decline from $\sim 4000$–$5000\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ to $\sim 2000\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$. Peak luminosity suggests $M_{\mathrm{BH}}\sim 10^{6}\,M_{\odot}$ with large uncertainty, and Swift/XRT detects $L_{X}\sim 10^{42}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ ($0.3$–$10\,\mathrm{keV}$) without intrinsic absorption.
papers.problem: The paper asks whether the feature near $5805\,\mathrm{\AA}$ in off-nuclear TDE 2025abcr is optical C IV $\lambda\lambda 5801,5812$, rather than shifted He I or [N II], and what its excitation implies for a compact, dense reprocessing region.
papers.method: The analysis combines ZTF forced-PSF and LCOGT difference-imaging photometry, GTC/HiPERCAM and LCOGT intranight monitoring, and Swift/XRT–UVOT data with six VLT/FORS2 spectra ($R\simeq 900$) and one NOT/ALFOSC spectrum ($R\sim 300$), calibrated to contemporaneous photometry and corrected for $E(B-V)=0.013\,\mathrm{mag}$. A flat $\Lambda$CDM cosmology is adopted, the continuum is fit by a single-temperature blackbody, and each line by concentric double-Lorentzian components. Non-variability at the $0.008\,\mathrm{mag}$ ($g$) and $0.025\,\mathrm{mag}$ ($u$) levels is used to infer $R\sim 10^{14}\,\mathrm{cm}$.
papers.reason: This off-nuclear TDE paper is relevant to photoionization and compact-object reprocessing, but it is not central to FRB, jet, neutrino, or supernova-engine work. Its useful increment is the optical C IV identification and the inferred compact reprocessing photosphere.

papers.title: Flux Variation of the Crab Pulsar Observed Using Fermi LAT and NuSTAR
papers.result: Pulsed Crab emission is not steady. The mean gamma-ray flux is $F_{\gamma}=(1.283\pm0.004)\times10^{-9}\,\mathrm{erg\,cm^{-2}\,s^{-1}}$ (0.1–100 GeV), with month-scale deviations from a few percent to $\sim20\%$, and $\Gamma_{\gamma}\approx2.17\pm0.02$ varying by up to $\sim10\%$. Linear slopes $(-2.65\pm0.94)\times10^{-12}\,\mathrm{erg\,cm^{-2}\,s^{-1}\,yr^{-1}}$ and $(-1.92\pm0.59)\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{yr^{-1}}$ are poor descriptions ($\chi^2_{\nu}=1.9$, $p=2.6\times10^{-14}$; $\chi^2_{\nu}=2.7$, $p=6.8\times10^{-32}$). The X-ray means are $F_{\rm X}=(6.086\pm0.002)\times10^{-9}\,\mathrm{erg\,cm^{-2}\,s^{-1}}$ and $\Gamma_{\rm X}=1.80\pm0.05$, with slopes $(-7.95\pm0.69)\times10^{-11}\,\mathrm{erg\,cm^{-2}\,s^{-1}\,yr^{-1}}$ and $(+5.37\pm1.95)\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{yr^{-1}}$. Flux and photon index are anti-correlated (brighter-when-harder), with $r_{\rm s}=-0.35$ ($p=4.0\times10^{-7}$) and $r_{\rm s}=-0.63$ ($p=5.5\times10^{-6}$). Nebular synchrotron, inverse-Compton, and total fluxes are not significantly correlated with the pulsed flux.
papers.problem: The work tests whether Crab pulsed high-energy emission is steady on timescales much longer than the rotation period, except for a smooth secular decline from pulsar aging, and how braking-index deviations could arise if $I$, $\mu$, or $\alpha$ change.
papers.method: Archival Fermi-LAT data (MJD 54710–60842, 100 MeV–100 GeV, about 17 yr, monthly integrals) and NuSTAR data (3.0–79.0 keV, about 13 yr) are phase-gated into pulsed and nebular spectra, with $1\sigma$ statistical plus systematic errors. Pulsed fits use $\mathrm{tbabs}\times\mathrm{powerlaw}$; nebular $N_{\rm H}=0.36\times10^{22}\,\mathrm{cm^{-2}}$ is fixed, $\Gamma_{\rm X}$ and normalization are tied within an epoch, and a 3% systematic uncertainty is included. Absorption uses the cited photoelectric cross sections. The braking index is $n=\Omega\ddot{\Omega}/\dot{\Omega}^{2}$, with spin parameters from the Jodrell Bank monthly ephemeris and $\ddot{\Omega}$ from adjacent $\dot{\Omega}$ differences. Magnetic-dipole spin-down power scales as $I\Omega\dot{\Omega}$.
papers.reason: This is a compact-object high-energy result: long-term Fermi-LAT and NuSTAR data show that Crab pulsed GeV and X-ray flux and photon index vary and are anti-correlated, testing the steady-pulsar assumption. It is incremental for magnetospheric emission and spin-down, but not central to FRB, supernova-engine, jet, or neutrino studies.

papers.title: Molecular signatures of shocked gas and enhanced cosmic-ray ionization in supernova remnant W49B revealed by ALMA
papers.result: Twelve western regions show HCO$^{+}$ and $^{12}$CO lines with FWHM $25$–$60\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$. Non-LTE analysis gives $n=(0.5$–$1.6)\times10^{5}\,\mathrm{cm^{-3}}$ and $N_{\rm HCO^{+}}/N_{\rm CO}=(4.2$–$14.5)\times10^{-4}$. Matching this ratio requires $\zeta_{\rm CR}$ of a few $\times10^{-14}$–$10^{-13}\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}$, compared with the standard $2.5\times10^{-17}\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}$. From $+75$ to $+100$ versus $+100$ to $+125\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$, the beam-averaged ratio rises from $(5.8\pm0.4)\times10^{-4}$ to $(8.5\pm0.8)\times10^{-4}$. With $t_{\rm loss}(E)\sim E/[L_{\rm p}(E)n_{\rm H_2}v(E)]$ and $n_{\rm H_2}=6.3\times10^{4}\,\mathrm{cm^{-3}}$, $10$ and $100\,\mathrm{MeV}$ protons cool in $\sim1.2$ and $\sim39\,\mathrm{yr}$; diffusion bounds are $D(10\,\mathrm{MeV})>2.8\times10^{24}$ and $D(100\,\mathrm{MeV})>8.0\times10^{22}\,\mathrm{cm^{2}\,s^{-1}}$. Clump kinetic energy exceeds cumulative cosmic-ray and X-ray heating, and cosmic-ray heating exceeds X-ray heating.
papers.problem: The relative contributions of shocks, radiation, and cosmic rays to supernova feedback on molecular clouds are poorly constrained; in W49B the previously unresolved HCO$^{+}$/$^{12}$CO intensity ratio is $1$–$2$ orders of magnitude above typical molecular clouds.
papers.method: ALMA 12 m/ACA and APEX map HCO$^{+}$ $J=1$–$0$, $3$–$2$, $4$–$3$ and $^{12}$CO $J=3$–$2$; imaging uses CASA tclean with hogbom, Briggs robust $=0.5$, and feathering, with line ratios at $8.5''$. RADEX non-LTE models and Paris–Durham steady planar shocks ($V_{\rm shock}=20$–$55\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$) are compared through MCMC, with proton losses $t_{\rm loss}(E)\sim E/[L_{\rm p}(E)n_{\rm H_2}v(E)]$.
papers.reason: Resolved SNR–molecular-cloud shocks and an elevated cosmic-ray ionization rate in W49B quantify supernova mechanical and cosmic-ray feedback, but the paper does not address central engines, shock breakout, jets, FRBs, or neutrinos.

papers.title: Log-normal behavior of Optical Polarization in a sample of Blazars: Evidence for Multiplicative Magneto-hydrodynamic Processes in Relativistic Jets
papers.result: For 10 blazars (3 BL Lacs and 7 FSRQs) with >100 Steward SPOL measurements each during 2008–2018 at $\lambda=500$–$700\,\mathrm{nm}$, V-band flux and $\mathrm{PD}=\sqrt{q^{2}+u^{2}}$ are generally better described by a log-normal distribution than by a Gaussian or Rice distribution. Exceptions are the flux of 3C 273 (Gaussian) and the PD of PKS 2155$-$304 (Rice). ZDCF flux–PD correlation peaks are about $0.53$–$0.93$; PD has high relative variability amplitude $\mathrm{RVA}=(F_{\rm max}-F_{\rm min})/F_{\rm max}$ and an approximately linear rms–PD trend. Successive perturbations $\vec{B}_{n+1}=\vec{B}_{n}(1+\delta_n)$ accumulate as $\vec{B}=\vec{B}_{0}\prod_{i=1}^{N}(1+\delta_i)$.
papers.problem: The physical origin of large optical polarization-degree changes in blazar jets is unclear: long-term flux variability is often ascribed to multiplicative processes because it is log-normal, but it is not established whether PD variability has the same origin rather than arising from linearly superposed independent zones.
papers.method: Daily Bayesian blocks ($p_0=0.01$) are applied to V-band flux and PD. Variability is quantified by $F_{\rm var}=\sqrt{(S^{2}-E^{2})/F^{2}}$, $F=\sigma_{\rm LC}^{2}/\sigma^{2}$ with critical value 6.636, RVA, and ANOVA. Gaussian, log-normal, and Rice models are compared using $\mathrm{AIC}=2k-2\ln(L)$, $\mathrm{BIC}=k\ln(n)-2\ln(L)$, Anderson–Darling tests, and $\chi_r^{2}$; the log-normal PDF is $f(x)=1/(x\sigma\sqrt{2\pi})\exp[-(\ln x-\mu)^{2}/(2\sigma^{2})]$. Interpretation uses transverse-shock, helical-field, and TEMZ models and $\partial\vec{B}/\partial t=\vec{\nabla}\times(\vec{v}\times\vec{B})+\eta\vec{\nabla}^{2}\vec{B}$.
papers.reason: The work links optical synchrotron polarization in blazar relativistic jets to multiplicative MHD variability, which is relevant to jet magnetic structure but peripheral to FRB, supernova-engine, and neutrino priorities.

papers.title: Two-component $γ$-Ray Structure from the CR Sources
papers.result: The baseline photon spectrum is $\frac{d\Phi_{\gamma}}{dE_{\gamma}}=\frac{d\Phi_{\pi^{0},\mathrm{re}}}{dE_{\gamma}}+\frac{d\Phi_{\mathrm{IC},\mathrm{fresh}}}{dE_{\gamma}}$. In low-density regions surrounded by dense molecular clumps the two components form clearly separated peaks; in a dense environment with an additional nearby clump they overlap more smoothly and the high-energy part is mainly a broad shoulder. The low-energy bump is primarily $\pi^{0}$ emission from background cosmic rays compressed and reaccelerated in dense clouds, while the harder high-energy component is usually inverse Compton from freshly accelerated electrons and can instead be hadronic when the gas density is high. The neutrino flux is predicted from the gamma-ray-constrained proton spectrum and is not a fixed fraction of the total gamma-ray flux. Reported source scales include CTB 80 at $d=2\,\mathrm{kpc}$, W44 at about $20\,\mathrm{kyr}$ and $2.2\,\mathrm{kpc}$, $\gamma$ Cygni at about $7\,\mathrm{kyr}$, $1.7\,\mathrm{kpc}$ and radius about $15\,\mathrm{pc}$, W51C at about $5.5\,\mathrm{kpc}$ with atomic-hydrogen density about $30$–$160\,\mathrm{cm^{-3}}$, and 1LHAASO J1852+0050u above $100\,\mathrm{TeV}$ with molecular-cloud density about $360\,\mathrm{cm^{-3}}$. Near HESS J1731-347 the diffusion coefficient can be about $3$–$20$ times below the usual Galactic-disk value.
papers.problem: The paper asks whether the two-component gamma-ray spectra of these cosmic-ray sources have a common physical origin and how the surrounding density structure changes the separation of the components.
papers.method: GALPROP supplies the spatially dependent background cosmic rays, with $D_{xx}(r,z,\mathcal{R})=D_{0}F(r,z)\,\beta^{\eta}(\mathcal{R}/\mathcal{R}_{0})^{\delta_{0}F(r,z)}$, $D_{0}=4.8\times10^{28}\,\mathrm{cm^{2}\,s^{-1}}$ and $\delta_{0}=0.63$. Shock reacceleration may be steepened by ion–neutral damping through $f_{\mathrm{sh}}(p)=f_{\mathrm{acc}}(p)\,\mathcal{B}(p)$, where $\mathcal{B}=1$ below $p_{\mathrm{br}}$ and $\mathcal{B}=p_{\mathrm{br}}/p$ above it. Compression $s\equiv n_m/n_d=n_m/(r_{\mathrm{sh}}n_0)$ maps momenta as $p\to s^{1/3}p$ and gives $n_{p,\mathrm{ad}}(p)=s^{2/3}n_{p,\mathrm{sh}}(s^{-1/3}p)$; accumulation then follows $\partial N_p/\partial t=\partial_p[b_p N_p]+Q_p$. Fresh particles supply the second component, and neutrinos are calculated from the same $p$–$p$ proton and gas model without a separate normalization.
papers.reason: The paper is useful for supernova-remnant shock–cloud interactions and multi-messenger tests because it ties two-component gamma-ray spectra to reaccelerated background protons and predicts pp neutrinos, but it is not centered on FRBs, central engines, or relativistic jets.

papers.title: NuSTAR view of the NGC 4151 corona: thermal balance and astroparticle constraints
papers.result: The hard X-ray continuum is thermal Comptonization with $kT_{\rm e}\approx 40-125$ keV and slab $\tau\approx 0.4-1.2$. $kT_{\rm e}$ and $\tau$ are anticorrelated at Compton parameter $\gamma\approx 3.12$ (historical $y\approx 1$; bright states $kT_{\rm e}\approx 40-100$ keV, $\tau\approx 1-2$). Variability gives $\tau_{\rm var}\approx 5-28$ h, $R\approx 250-1200\,r_g$ and $\ell\approx 0.5-3.7$, below pair runaway. $L_\nu/L_X\approx 3\times 10^{-3}$ does not displace Compton cooling. For $\sim 8.5$ MeV X17 $e^\pm$ injection, $t_{\rm th}\sim 0.82-24$ h exceeds Compton cooling ($0.07-0.45$ h); extra pairs do not change $kT_{\rm e}$ or $\tau$ unless injection greatly exceeds photoproduction.
papers.problem: What sets the thermal balance of the NGC 4151 hot corona, and can neutrino losses or X17-induced pairs alter the observed $kT_{\rm e}$–$\tau$ thermostat?
papers.method: Fourteen NuSTAR spectra were reduced in HEASoft (60 arcsec source region, background subtraction, 3600 s light curves) and fit with tbabs+zpcfabs+nthcomp+pexrav+zgauss. Slab $\tau$ is derived from $\Gamma$ and $kT_{\rm e}$ with the Sunyaev & Titarchuk (1980) relation, avoiding the spherical Eq. (14) factor of 3. Flux changes $>3\sigma$ define $\tau_{\rm var}$, then $R<c\tau_{\rm var}/(1+z)$ and $\ell=\sigma_T L_X/(R m_e c^3)$. X17 effects are judged by comparing Coulomb $t_{\rm th}$ and photoproduced $n_\pm$ from slab $u_{\rm rad}$ with the Compton cooling time.
papers.reason: This NuSTAR study of the NGC 4151 corona is adjacent to the group's neutrino and compact high-energy interests: it quantifies thermal Compton balance and tests whether neutrinos or X17 pairs can compete with Compton cooling, but it is not an FRB, supernova-engine, or jet-breakout paper.

papers.title: Unveiling the Extreme Universe with Recent IACT Discoveries
papers.result: RS Oph kept a stable differential spectrum from $\sim 50\,\mathrm{GeV}$ to a few hundred GeV on days 1, 2, and 4, with fixed index and normalization through a multi-day plateau before decaying in step with the GeV and optical light. SS 433 is fit by electrons at $\sim 100$–$200\,\mathrm{TeV}$ cooling in $B\approx 10$–$20\,\mu\mathrm{G}$; Vela’s hard pulse runs from $100\,\mathrm{GeV}$ to $20\,\mathrm{TeV}$ and needs $\gamma_e\sim 10^{7}$ outside $R_{\rm LC}\approx 4.3\times 10^{7}\,\mathrm{m}$. LST-1 prefers a Galactic-center ridge cutoff $E_{\rm cut}\approx 24\,\mathrm{TeV}$, against an earlier uncutoff spectrum to $\sim 50\,\mathrm{TeV}$ that had required protons to $\sim 1\,\mathrm{PeV}$.
papers.problem: Which sites and channels produce $E\gtrsim 50\,\mathrm{GeV}$ photons in novae, microquasar jets, and pulsars, when curvature radiation is expected to cut off near a few GeV and $\mathrm{d}N/\mathrm{d}E\propto E^{-\Gamma}$ ($\Gamma\gtrsim 2$) plus an area $\lesssim 1\,\mathrm{m}^{2}$ limits Fermi-LAT above $\sim 100\,\mathrm{GeV}$?
papers.method: IACTs use the atmosphere as a calorimeter, with nanosecond Cherenkov light giving $A_{\rm eff}\sim 10^{5}\,\mathrm{m}^{2}$. RS Oph is interpreted by DSA of a power-law proton spectrum with a smooth exponential cutoff at a few hundred GeV; shower reconstruction is shifting from Hillas parameters to CTLearn CNNs and GNNs on calibrated pixel charge and arrival time near $\lesssim 50\,\mathrm{GeV}$.
papers.reason: This IACT review reports nova–wind shocks with a multi-day VHE plateau, microquasar jet cooling, pulsar emission outside the light cylinder, and GRB afterglows, which bear on relativistic outflows and compact-object acceleration, but it is a broad survey rather than a focused test of one group hypothesis.

papers.title: Perturbative QCD Constraints on Hot Neutron-Star Matter
papers.result: Along fixed-$\hat{s}$ adiabats the allowed region shrinks monotonically as temperature rises. For DD2 the exit density falls from $n^{*}\simeq 1.0\,\mathrm{fm^{-3}}$ at $\hat{s}=0$ to $n^{*}\simeq 0.74\,\mathrm{fm^{-3}}$ at $\hat{s}=5$, below the cold maximum-mass central density $n_{\mathrm{B}}^{c}\simeq 0.85\,\mathrm{fm^{-3}}$. At $6\,n_{\rm sat}$, 4, 5, and 7 of 11 RMF models are excluded for $\hat{s}\le 1$, $\hat{s}=2$, and $\hat{s}=4$. Half-exclusion of the Bayesian samples occurs at $\hat{s}_{50}\simeq 3.4$ (DDH) and $\hat{s}_{50}\simeq 4.4$ (NL); by $\hat{s}=5$ essentially all DDH and $\sim 90\%$ of NL samples are excluded. The DD2/DD-MEX exit boundary runs from $(\mu_{\mathrm{B}},T)\simeq(2.16\,\mathrm{GeV},0)$ to $(1.55\,\mathrm{GeV},152\,\mathrm{MeV})$, crossing $n_{\mathrm{B}}^{c}=0.85\,\mathrm{fm^{-3}}$ at $T\simeq 125\,\mathrm{MeV}$.
papers.problem: The model-independent pQCD equation-of-state bound had been established only for cold, catalyzed matter, leaving open whether it constrains the hot, dense matter in binary neutron-star mergers, core-collapse supernovae, and proto-neutron stars.
papers.method: The Komoltsev–Kurkela construction is applied on adiabats of fixed $\hat{s}\equiv s/n_{\mathrm{B}}$ after replacing $\mu_{\mathrm{B}}$ by the specific enthalpy $h=(\varepsilon+p)/n_{\mathrm{B}}=\mu_{\mathrm{B}}+T\hat{s}$, using $\mathrm{d}p=n_{\mathrm{B}}\,\mathrm{d}h$ and $c_{s}^{2}=(\mathrm{d}\ln h/\mathrm{d}\ln n_{\mathrm{B}})_{\hat{s}}$. The low anchor is HS(DD2) at $n_{\mathrm{B}}=0.176\,\mathrm{fm^{-3}}$ and the high anchor is scale-averaged pQCD at $n_{\mathrm{B}}=6.5\,\mathrm{fm^{-3}}$, with $\bar{\Lambda}=\sqrt{(0.722\times 4\pi T X_{\mathrm{lat}})^{2}+(2\mu_{\mathrm{B}}X/3)^{2}}$ log-uniformly averaged over $X\in[0.5,2.0]$. Closed-form $(h,n_{\mathrm{B}})$ and $(\varepsilon,p)$ boundaries are tested on 11 RMF models and 500 samples from each of the DDH and NL posteriors.
papers.reason: The work gives a model-independent finite-entropy pQCD bound on the hot EOS sampled in neutron-star mergers and proto-neutron stars, which is useful for compact-object multimessenger modeling, but it does not directly address FRBs, jets, neutrinos, or shock breakout.

papers.title: Analysis Methodology of the Search for Ultrahigh Energy Neutrinos in 10.6 Years of Askaryan Radio Array Data
papers.result: With an effective livetime of $10.6$ yr ($25.9$ station-years after quality cuts), no neutrino candidate remains. The single phased-array event ($\mathrm{SNR}\sim 12$, elevation $-35^\circ$) is local A5 detector emission. The expected background is $0.13\pm 0.01\,(\mathrm{stat.})^{+0.05}_{-0.06}\,(\mathrm{syst.})$, from $b_{\mathrm{surf}}=4.50^{+1.01}_{-0.85}\times 10^{-2}$ and $b_{\mathrm{therm}}=8.65^{+0.44}_{-0.28}\times 10^{-2}$, giving a $5\sigma$ threshold $n_{\mathrm{disc}}=4$. Analysis efficiency is $28\%$ for a flux at current experimental upper limits. The $90\%$ CL all-flavor limit is the strongest reported at $50$–$1000\,\mathrm{EeV}$ and excludes the Muzio trans-GZK model. Analysis-level expectations are Global UL $5.3$ ($\epsilon=27.6\%$), Muzio $2.4$ ($21.8\%$), Kotera $0.4$ ($21.1\%$), $100\%$ protons $0.2$ ($25.0\%$), Fang pulsars $0.2$ ($16.7\%$), and KM3NeT $1.6$ ($13.8\%$).
papers.problem:
Whether a diffuse flux of ultrahigh-energy neutrinos, $E_
u\gtrsim 100\,\mathrm{PeV}$, including cosmogenic neutrinos from UHECR interactions with the CMB and EBL, is detectable through in-ice Askaryan radio pulses. UHECRs ($E_{\mathrm{CR}}\gtrsim 1\,\mathrm{EeV}$) are mostly extragalactic heavy nuclei whose magnetic deflections block source tracing, while protons are GZK-suppressed above $\sim 10^{19.7}\,\mathrm{eV}$; near $1\,\mathrm{EeV}$, IceCube and ANITA give $E_
u^2\Phi_
u\lesssim 10^{-8}\,\mathrm{GeV}\,\mathrm{cm}^{-2}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}\,\mathrm{sr}^{-1}$.
papers.method: Five ARA stations (2013–2023) are analyzed with $10\%$ of data for background design and $90\%$ blinded. NuLeptonSim generates $E^{-1}$ neutrinos from $10^{16}$–$10^{21}\,\mathrm{eV}$ for later reweighting inside a fiducial cylinder, using Connolly cross sections and PREM; AraSim models the stations. AraProc22 calibrates waveforms and applies a $50$–$875\,\mathrm{MHz}$ bandpass. Signal strength is $\mathrm{SNR}=(V_{\mathrm{pp}}/2)/\mathrm{RMS}$. Direction uses $C_{ij}(\tau)$ with $n(z)=n_{\mathrm{ice}}-(n_{\mathrm{ice}}-n_{\mathrm{firn}})e^{-z/\Lambda}$ ($n_{\mathrm{ice}}=1.780$, $n_{\mathrm{firn}}=1.326$, $\Lambda\simeq 49.505\,\mathrm{m}$). Phased-array beams scale as signal $\propto N$ and noise $\propto\sqrt{N}$. Cuts minimize the $5\sigma$ discovery normalization at $E_0=10^{18.5}\,\mathrm{eV}$, $$\phi_0^{\mathrm{disc}}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma},\boldsymbol{\Theta})=\frac{\mathrm{FC}(n_{\mathrm{disc}}(B),B)}{\int f(E)\,\mathcal{E}(E)\,dE}.$$ Thermal separation uses impulsivity $\mathcal{I}=2\langle H\rangle-1$.
papers.reason: This five-station ARA diffuse-flux search is relevant because its null result and 90% CL limits test cosmogenic and compact-object (trans-GZK and pulsar) neutrino scenarios, but it is mainly an analysis-methodology update rather than a source-physics result on FRBs, supernova engines, or jets.

papers.title: Spectral-Timing Evolution of the Black Hole X-ray Binary LMC X-3: An XPoSat View
papers.result: Between the 2024 and 2025 XSPECT campaigns the source moved from a harder, fainter, more variable interval to a brighter, softer, less variable state. Epoch-averaged fits of $\mathrm{tbabs}\times\mathrm{diskbb}$ give $kT_{\rm in}=0.837\pm0.005\,\mathrm{keV}$ (2024, soft segment only; $N_{\rm H}$ frozen at $0.01\times10^{22}\,\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$) and $kT_{\rm in}=1.167\pm0.004\,\mathrm{keV}$ (2025), with unabsorbed flux rising from $(1.964\pm0.002)$ to $(9.585\pm0.004)\times10^{-10}\,\mathrm{erg}\,\mathrm{cm}^{-2}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ (about fivefold). Disk normalizations are $24.8\pm0.7$ and $29.1\pm0.5$. The 2024 PDS has excess power below $\sim0.05\,\mathrm{Hz}$; neither epoch shows a significant QPO or soft–hard lag. For $D\sim50\,\mathrm{kpc}$ and $i\sim67^{\circ}$, the 2025 normalization implies an apparent inner radius $\sim43\,\mathrm{km}$ and a corrected radius $\sim50\,\mathrm{km}$, close to an ISCO of $\sim53\,\mathrm{km}$ for $M\sim7\,M_{\odot}$ and $a_{\ast}\approx0.25$.
papers.problem: How the luminosity, spectral hardness, and rapid variability of persistent LMC X–3 change between the 2024 and 2025 XSPECT epochs, and whether that change is the usual shift toward a stable, thermally dominated disk.
papers.method: Public Level-2 XSPECT data (0.8–15 keV; analysis uses $2^{\circ}\times2^{\circ}$ detectors) were flare-filtered, merged by epoch, and reduced with the standard pipeline. Hardness is the 2.0–10.0 keV to 0.8–2.0 keV count-rate ratio on 500 s bins; HIDs and hardness–rms diagrams use sigma-clipped light curves. PDS use the Belloni fractional-rms normalization, and soft–hard delays use 10 ms cross-correlation. Spectra are fit in XSPEC 12.14 with $\chi^{2}$ and 68% errors; the adopted model is $\mathrm{tbabs}\times\mathrm{diskbb}$, while $\mathrm{tbabs}\times\mathrm{powerlaw}$ and $\mathrm{tbabs}\times(\mathrm{diskbb}+\mathrm{powerlaw})$ fit worse. The disk normalization is $\mathrm{Norm}_{\rm disk}=\left(\frac{R_{\rm in}/\mathrm{km}}{D/10\,\mathrm{kpc}}\right)^{2}\cos i$.
papers.reason: This is a standard XPoSat/XSPECT spectral–timing study of thermal accretion-state evolution in the persistent black-hole HMXB LMC X–3. It has no substantial link to FRB/PRS, supernova central engines, shock breakout, CSM interaction, relativistic jets, neutrinos, or dispersion-measure physics.

papers.title: Revisiting the Neutrino Emission and Physical Parameter Constraints from Time-Resolved Spectra of Gamma-Ray Bursts
papers.result: Summed time-resolved spectra change the expected muon-neutrino counts relative to time-integrated spectra. For GRB 080916C the counts are about $2.46\times 10^{-7}$ versus $1.97\times 10^{-7}$, with a high-$R$, high-$\Gamma$ ratio $\sim 1.25$ and a low-$R$, low-$\Gamma$ ratio $\sim 0.9$. GRB 110721A gives $\sim 5.30\times 10^{-4}$ versus $\sim 5.49\times 10^{-4}$ (everywhere $<10^{-3}$; ratios $\sim 1.4$ and $\sim 0.7$). GRB 090902B gives $\sim 1.31\times 10^{-3}$ versus $\sim 1.01\times 10^{-3}$ (factor $\sim 1.3$; model-independent estimate still $<3\times 10^{-2}$; ratios $\sim 2.1$ and $\sim 0.9$). For GRB 221009A, an ICMART case $R=10^{16}\,\mathrm{cm}$, $\Gamma=500$, $\varepsilon_p/\varepsilon_e=3$ yields $\sim 1.02\times 10^{-1}$ versus $\sim 3.36\times 10^{-2}$. At fixed $R\simeq 1.07\times 10^{15}\,\mathrm{cm}$, time-resolved non-detection gives $\Gamma>254,371,537$ for $\varepsilon_p/\varepsilon_e=1,3,10$, compared with $\Gamma>188,273,395$ from the time-integrated spectrum, i.e. lower limits higher by $28\%$–$40\%$.
papers.problem: Non-detection of GRB high-energy neutrinos can bound the jet, but duration-averaged time-integrated spectra do not follow spectral evolution and need not represent the emission-zone conditions sampled by time-resolved spectra.
papers.method: Prompt-only $p\gamma$ calculations in the Yuan et al. framework use observed spectral parameters together with $E_{p,\rm iso}=(\varepsilon_p/\varepsilon_e)E_{\rm\gamma,iso}$, $L_{B,\rm iso}=(\varepsilon_B/\varepsilon_e)L_{\rm\gamma,iso}$ and $E_{\rm\gamma,iso}=L_{\rm\gamma,iso}\times\Delta t/(1+z)$, and the IceCube 14-year muon-track effective area. GRB 221009A is split into 43 GECAM-C Band intervals; model-independent $R$–$\Gamma$ limits are compared with the internal-shock radius $R_{\rm IS}=2\Gamma^{2}c\delta t_{\rm min}/(1+z)$ at $\delta t_{\rm min}=0.01\,\mathrm{s}$, using $N_{\rm sig}=2.3$ (90% C.L.).
papers.reason: The paper quantitatively revises IceCube neutrino yields and jet-parameter bounds for bright GRBs by replacing duration-averaged spectra with time-resolved spectra, directly relevant to relativistic jets and high-energy neutrinos.

papers.title: Fast Radio Burst Population Constrained by Source-Count Growth and Burst Clustering
papers.result: Source counts grow linearly: β_s = 0.98 ± 0.02, β_r = 1.06 ± 0.14, Γ_rs = 1.08^{+0.14}_{-0.16}, Q = 0.026^{+0.004}_{-0.006}; rate distribution follows φ(r) ∝ r^{-α} with α = 2.06 ± 0.14 (or 1.975^{+0.005}_{-0.004}); stationary clustering fails while on/off activity with duty cycle ≲ 0.2 fits; apparent repeater fraction does not measure true repeating fraction.
papers.problem: Whether FRB sources are all repeaters obeying a single rate distribution or include a genuine one-off population; reconciling source-count slopes, repeat fraction Q, and observed clustering.
papers.method: Exposure-corrected cumulative counts N(Δt) = ∑ 1/f_i with f_i = T_eff(δ_i)/T_survey; power-law rate distribution φ(r) ∝ r^{-α} (1 < α < 2 yields count-count slope = 1); Weibull clustering and on/off activity windows evaluated via analytic P_{≥2}^{win} and Monte Carlo; broken power-law and two-population extensions tested.
papers.reason: Paper directly constrains FRB source population via CHIME Catalog 2 source-count growth (linear β_s, β_r) and repeat clustering, yielding rate index α ≃ 2 and requiring long-term on/off activity rather than stationary clustering.

papers.title: Detection of 2 MeV spectral bump and ~40 MeV emission line from GRB 221009A
papers.result: CSES-01/HEPP-H cross-calibrated with unsaturated GECAM-C recovers the 2–255 MeV evolution of GRB 221009A ($z=0.151$, $E_{\mathrm{iso}}\sim1.5\times10^{55}\,\mathrm{erg}$). A $\sim2\,\mathrm{MeV}$ bump is present at the first peak; at $T_{\mathrm{ref}}+230$–$231\,\mathrm{s}$, $L_{\mathrm{iso}}\sim1.1\times10^{54}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$, and the surrounding $10\,\mathrm{s}$ gives $E_{\mathrm{iso}}\sim4.9\times10^{54}\,\mathrm{erg}$ (rest-frame $1\,\mathrm{keV}$–$10\,\mathrm{MeV}$). The thermal part is only $\sim6\%$ ($kT_{\mathrm{ph}}\simeq2\,\mathrm{MeV}$, $F_{\mathrm{bump}}\sim2\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}\,cm^{-2}}$, $L_{\mathrm{ph}}\simeq10^{53}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$, $E_{\mathrm{therm,iso}}=9\times10^{53}\,\mathrm{erg}$, $r_0\sim10^{7}\,\mathrm{cm}$), so the bulk is attributed to magnetic energy. A narrow line centered near $37\,\mathrm{MeV}$ starts near $40\,\mathrm{MeV}$ and follows $E_{\mathrm{line}}\propto(t-t_0)^{-1.05}$ with $t_0=T_{\mathrm{ref}}+226\,\mathrm{s}$ and $k=-1.05^{+0.22}_{-0.17}$. Its radius is $r\approx2.45\times10^{16}(\Gamma/500)\,\mathrm{cm}$; $F_{\mathrm{line}}\propto(t-t_0)^{1.86\pm0.38}$ early and $\propto(t-t_0)^{-2.16}$ late, not the pure-curvature $F_{\mathrm{line}}\propto(t-t_0)^{-3}$. Global significance is $>4.4\sigma$ ($\Delta\mathrm{cstat}=91.30$, $P<4.3\times10^{-6}$).
papers.problem: At the peak of GRB 221009A, conventional detectors saturate and Compton and pair events overlap, leaving a MeV–sub-GeV gap exactly where one must test whether the prompt outflow is thermally or magnetically dominated and what produces the drifting MeV line.
papers.method: HEPP-H is gain-corrected, background-subtracted with six pre-burst orbits, $\bar{R}=\frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^{m}N_i/t_i$ ($m=6$), and dead-time corrected by $N=n/(1-n\tau)$ with $\tau\approx240\,\mu\mathrm{s}$. Because that correction only partially linearizes the peak, photon arrival is Monte Carlo sampled with $p(\Delta t_n)=\lambda\exp(-\lambda\Delta t_n)$ and $\lambda=R_{\mathrm{in}}$ to build a dynamic response. Continua use $A_{\mathrm{PL}}(E)=KE^{-\alpha}$, broken power laws, CPL, and Band, plus blackbody and Gaussian terms ranked by AIC. Sliding windows, GEANT4 matrices, and $\sigma_{\mathrm{S}}^{2}=\sigma_{\mathrm{rsp}}^{2}+\sigma_{\mathrm{DCP}}^{2}+\sigma_{\mathrm{BG}}^{2}$ ($\sigma_{\mathrm{S}}\approx9.9\%$) assess the line.
papers.reason: Unsaturated 2–255 MeV spectroscopy of GRB 221009A directly constrains prompt jet composition, separating a sub-dominant photosphere from magnetically powered emission and an evolving MeV annihilation line.

papers.title: What stands behind luminosity peak of type IIP supernovae?
papers.result: For SN 1999em the initial broad peak is reproduced by an RSG with a hydrogen envelope steeper than evolutionary models: an outer layer of about $0.9\,M_{\odot}$ with $k=d\ln\rho/d\ln r<-3$. MCMC optima are $R_{pSN}=680^{+46}_{-37}\,R_{\odot}$, $M_{ej}=21.9\pm0.7\,M_{\odot}$, $E=(1.45\pm0.07)\times10^{51}\,\mathrm{erg}$, and $M_{\mathrm{Ni}}=0.036\,M_{\odot}$. VELTEM gives $R_{\mathrm{base}}=62\,R_{\odot}$, $R_{ip}=363\,R_{\odot}$, $\alpha=0.52$, and $\beta=5.35$. By the Sedov criterion the shock accelerates where $\rho r^{3}$ decreases, i.e. $k<-3$, for $r>100\,R_{\odot}$, fitting the first $\sim30$ days and a maximum velocity $13500\pm500\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$. A shell $\gtrsim0.3\,M_{\odot}$ can supply the peak but decelerates the outer ejecta. Runs started at $M_{ej}=9\,M_{\odot}$ and $E=0.6\times10^{51}\,\mathrm{erg}$ return to a massive, energetic solution; progenitors significantly below $\sim21\,M_{\odot}$ are excluded.
papers.problem: One-dimensional explosions of evolutionary red supergiants do not reproduce the initial broad pre-plateau luminosity peak of SNe IIP such as SN 1999em and lack composition-interface mixing, while an added CSM shell conflicts with early spectra; observed IIP progenitors below $15\,M_{\odot}$ are also missing.
papers.method: Spherically symmetric Lagrangian radiation hydrodynamics with $P=P_g+E_r/3$, $E_r=aT^4$, Rosseland diffusion, and flux limiter $f(\xi)=(2+3\xi)/(2+3\xi+3\xi^2)$. The envelope is $k(r)=k_0(r/r_0)^p$ with $p=\alpha$ inside $R_{ip}$ and $p=\beta$ outside. Equilibrium-diffusion VELTEM, about $300$ times faster than CRAB, is sampled by Metropolis-Hastings MCMC in $R_{pSN}$, $M_{ej}$, $E$, $M_{\mathrm{mix}}$, $R_{ip}$, $\alpha$, and $\beta$ ($7000$ and $10000$ steps); $^{56}\mathrm{Ni}$ is fixed by the tail. Models are scored by $\chi^2$ against the bolometric light curve, H$\beta$ and Fe II 5169 Å photospheric velocities, and the H$\alpha$ blue-edge maximum velocity. The explosion is started by a supersonic piston at the $1.58\,M_{\odot}$ core boundary.
papers.reason: The work targets the pre-plateau luminosity peak of SNe IIP, contrasting shock propagation in a steep hydrogen-envelope density gradient with a massive CSM shell, which is directly useful for shock-breakout, plateau, and progenitor-structure studies.

papers.title: What the X-ray Emission from Young Supernovae Can Tell Us About Their Progenitors
papers.result: Wind density follows $\rho_w\propto\dot{M}/v_w$. In the Chevalier (1982) model, $\rho_{\mathrm{SN}}=\rho_0(v/v_0)^{-n}(t/t_0)^{-3}$, $\rho_{\mathrm{CSM}}\propto r^{-s}$ with $s=2$ for a steady wind, and $R_{\mathrm{CD}}\propto t^m$ where $m=(n-3)/(n-s)\le1$. For spherical progenitors with $9\le n\le12$, steady-wind thermal $L_x$ falls roughly as $t^{-0.7}$–$t^{-0.8}$ and approaches $t^{-1}$ at larger $n$. The order-of-magnitude luminosity is $L_i=3\times10^{39}g_{ff}C_n(\dot{M}_{-5}/v_{w1})^2(t/10\,\mathrm{d})^{-1}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$, with $C_n=1$ for the forward shock and $C_n=(n-3)(n-4)^2/[4(n-2)]$ for the reverse shock; observations constrain $\dot{M}/v_w$. RSG/IIP rates are $\dot{M}\approx10^{-8}$–$10^{-6}\,M_{\odot}\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, while WR Ib/c winds have $v_w\approx1000$–$3000\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$. Many sources show only $1$–$2\,\mathrm{keV}$, below $\sim40\,\mathrm{keV}$ expected for a $\sim5000\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ forward shock, favoring reverse-shock emission. SN 1993J has early $\dot{M}>10^{-5}\,M_{\odot}\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$; inverse-Compton modeling with $N(E)\propto E^{-p}$ at $p=3$ gives SN 2011ja $(1.2\pm0.2)\times10^{-7}\,M_{\odot}\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$; SN 2011dh is an adiabatic reverse shock with $\dot{M}$ of a few $\times10^{-6}\,M_{\odot}\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$. Thermal X-rays are directly proportional to circumstellar density, and a radiative reverse shock can coexist with a non-radiative forward shock.
papers.problem: The core problem is how X-rays from a young supernova shock expanding in a progenitor wind, rather than pristine ISM, can recover the progenitor mass-loss rate, wind velocity, and CSM density structure despite shock-type and geometry degeneracies.
papers.method: The analysis uses the Chevalier self-similar shock solution, with ambient density $\rho_{am}=\dot{M}(r_0/r)^s/(4\pi r_0^2 v_w)$, thermal-luminosity scalings for adiabatic and radiative shocks, inverse-Compton spectra $N(E)\propto E^{-p}$, and multiwavelength checks. Radio light curves are fit with Chevalier/Weiler relations to estimate $\dot{M}/v_w$, while optical/IR/UV emission is compared using $L_{\mathrm{opt/IR/UV}}=0.5\,\epsilon\,(\dot{M}/v_w)\,v_{\mathrm{sh}}^3$; X-ray light curves and spectra are preferred because self-similar evolution gives $v\propto t^{m-1}$.
papers.reason: This review directly links young-supernova X-rays to progenitor winds, shock–CSM interaction, and pre-explosion mass-loss history, and it provides scaling relations that can test those hypotheses.

papers.title: Jet energetics and remnant magnetism in short gamma-ray bursts from binary neutron-star mergers: A statistical study via broadband afterglow modeling
papers.result: For the 15 strictly constrained (SC) bursts, the median on-axis energy is $\log E_0=52.54$ (68% interval $[51.08,53.43]$), i.e. $E_0\simeq 3.5\times 10^{52}\,\mathrm{erg}$. The beaming-corrected kinetic energy has median $\log E_{\rm k}=49.58$, or $E_{\rm k}\simeq 3.8\times 10^{49}\,\mathrm{erg}$ (68% interval $[5.1\times 10^{48},1.9\times 10^{50}]\,\mathrm{erg}$), and the radiative efficiency has median $\eta_\gamma\simeq 0.35$ (68% interval $[0.09,0.79]$), where $\eta_\gamma=E_\gamma/(E_\gamma+E_{\rm k})$ and $\Gamma_0=300$. Under the BZ scaling $\frac{L_{\rm k}}{1-\eta_\gamma}\approx 10^{51}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}\left(\frac{a}{0.9}\right)^2\left(\frac{M_{\rm BH}}{5\,M_\odot}\right)^2\left(\frac{B_{\rm BH}}{10^{16}\,\mathrm{G}}\right)^2$, the SC horizon field is $B_{\rm BH}\simeq 7\times 10^{15}\,\mathrm{G}$ ($7.1^{+15.8}_{-4.8}\times 10^{15}\,\mathrm{G}$ and $7.2^{+16.3}_{-4.9}\times 10^{15}\,\mathrm{G}$ for the two $\tilde\Lambda$ cases), with amplification $\eta_B\equiv B_{\rm BH}/B_{\rm NS}$ of order $10^3$ (medians $1463$ and $1026$). For all 40 bursts the medians shift to $\log(E_0/\mathrm{erg})=52.35$, $\log(E_{\rm k}/\mathrm{erg})=50.20$, $\eta_\gamma=0.26$ and $B_{\rm BH}\sim 2\times 10^{16}\,\mathrm{G}$ ($\log(B_{\rm BH}/\mathrm{G})=16.31$–$16.36$).
papers.problem: The paper asks what beaming-corrected kinetic energies and gamma-ray efficiencies characterize cosmological short GRBs from BNS mergers, and what black-hole horizon field is required if the Blandford–Znajek process supplies most of the jet energy.
papers.method: Forty sGRBs with reliable redshifts (Gold Sample, $P_{\rm cc}<0.02$) are fitted burst by burst with an off-axis truncated Gaussian jet in a uniform ISM using afterglowpy, retaining only forward-shock points after removing intervals possibly affected by energy injection, flares, reverse shocks or kilonovae. The angular structure and beam-corrected energy are $E(\theta)=E_0\exp(-\theta^2/2\theta_{\rm c}^2)$ and $E_{\rm k}=E_0\theta_{\rm c}^2\left(1-e^{-\theta_{\rm w}^2/2\theta_{\rm c}^2}\right)$, while $E_{\gamma,\mathrm{iso}}=k\times 4\pi d_{\rm L}^2 f_\gamma/(1+z)$ with a population-mean $k=5$ when the spectrum is unavailable. The 15 SC posteriors supply empirical priors for the other 25 bursts. Jet power is then mapped to the horizon field through $L_{\rm BZ}=\frac{\kappa}{4\pi c}\Omega_{\rm H}^2\Phi_{\rm BH}^2 f(\Omega_{\rm H})$ with $\kappa\sim 0.05$, $\Omega_{\rm H}=ac/(2r_{\rm H})$, $E_{\rm BZ}=E_{\rm k}+E_\gamma$ and $L_{\rm k}\equiv E_{\rm k}/T_{90}$.
papers.reason: This statistical afterglow study directly constrains sGRB jet energy and the horizon magnetic field of BNS-merger black holes, which is central to relativistic-jet and compact-remnant engine physics. The reported $E_{\rm k}$, $\eta_\gamma$ and $B_{\rm BH}$ distributions can test whether a Blandford–Znajek engine is viable.

papers.title: Double Blandford: Resistive GRMHD simulations of accreting black holes simultaneously launch winds and jets
papers.result: All simulations form jets and winds; jets parabolic with $x \propto z^{\mathcal{K}}$ ($\mathcal{K}\approx0.52-0.64$); $\phi\lesssim15$; $P^{\rm BZ}/\dot{M}\approx0.49$ for $a_*=-0.9375$; $P^{\rm BP}/P^{\rm BZ}\approx30\%-35\%$ (constant with $\beta$), rising to $\approx99.5\%$ at $a_*=0.5$; high-$\sigma$ wind reaches $\Gamma_\infty\approx25$ but lacks mass loading; SANE/MAD states distinguished by $\sigma_\Phi/\bar{\Phi}$.
papers.problem: Ideal GRMHD cannot sustain large-scale poloidal field needed for BP disk winds while launching BZ jets; question is whether resistive thin-disk GRMHD permits simultaneous, observationally consistent jet+wind launching.
papers.method: Resistive GRMHD in BHAC on Kerr-Schild coordinates with $\eta(r,\theta)=0.50pt\,c_s\exp[-2(r\cos\theta/100pt)^2]$, cooling $L=\xi\Omega_K p/(\hat\gamma-1)(Y-1+|Y-1|)$, initial $\beta=1-10$, $H/R=0.05-0.1$, $a_*=\pm0.9375,0.5$; MAD parameter $\phi=\Phi/\sqrt{\dot{M}}$; outflow classification by outermost horizon-anchored field line and $Be>0$; power decomposed into EM/PAKE/EN components.
papers.reason: Paper directly simulates simultaneous BZ jet and BP wind launching from thin accretion disks using resistive GRMHD, yielding quantitative power ratios, geometries and efficiencies relevant to relativistic outflows around compact objects.

papers.title: Type Ia-CSM Supernovae. I. Uniform Light-Curve Characterization and Inference on the Underlying Type Ia Explosions
papers.result: SNe Ia-CSM are photometrically more uniform than interacting SNe IIn and track the luminous-slow IIn template rather than the faint-fast one. Median peak luminosities are thermal $(3.8^{+2.5}_{-1.8})\times10^{43}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ and optical $(2.3^{+1.4}_{-1.0})\times10^{43}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ (ratio $\sim1.6$), with $L_{\rm peak}<10^{44}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ and median $\widetilde{M}_{r,\rm peak}=-20.08$ mag. The $r$-band median timescales are $\widetilde{t}_{\rm rise50}=27.3$ day and $\widetilde{t}_{\rm decl50}=58.6$ day, with $t_{\rm decl50}\approx2\times t_{\rm rise50}$, $t_{\rm decl50}\approx4\times t_{\rm rise20}$, and $t_{\rm decl80}\approx1.5\times t_{\rm rise80}$; the 50% total $r$-band timescale is $87.0^{+75.5}_{-28.1}$ day. Radiated energy is bimodal: a dominant family $\sim(1-5)\times10^{50}$ erg on $\sim100$ day and a secondary family about one decade fainter on $\sim50$ day (50%-flux medians $1.4\times10^{50}$ erg optical and $2.5\times10^{50}$ erg thermal). Adopting $0.2<L_{\rm Ia}/L_{\rm SN}<0.7$ and $E_{\rm KE}=1.3\times10^{51}$ erg gives $E_{\rm rad}=\epsilon_{\rm rad}E_{\rm KE}$ with $\epsilon_{\rm rad}\approx0.1-0.6$, consistent with CSM masses $\sim2-11\,M_\odot$ and ejecta $\sim1.4\,M_\odot$. When $M_{\rm CSM}$ exceeds the ejecta mass, $v\approx\sqrt{2E_{\rm KE}/M_{\rm CSM}}\approx4500\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}(E_{\rm KE}/10^{51}\,\mathrm{erg})^{1/2}(M_{\rm CSM}/5\,M_\odot)^{-1/2}$. Inferred underlying events run from 1991T-like through normal/2002es-like to 1991bg-like (and possibly 2003fg-like).
papers.problem: How uniform are Ia-CSM light curves relative to SNe IIn, what peak luminosity, timescale, and radiated energy do they have, and which underlying thermonuclear subtypes and progenitor delays can supply the dense hydrogen-rich CSM?
papers.reason: This is the largest uniform optical sample of thermonuclear SNe Ia-CSM and directly constrains CSM-interaction timescales, radiated energy, and the underlying Ia engine. It is relevant to SN–CSM interaction studies but is not a high-energy, jet, neutrino, or shock-breakout result.

papers.title: New Physics in Ultra-High-Energy Neutrino Flavor
papers.result: UHE flavor ratios are projected to be the most sensitive probe of LIV for operators with $d\ge 4$, improving current bounds by up to twenty orders of magnitude, and by up to $\sim 20$ orders for $d=8$. Over $100\,\mathrm{PeV}$–$10\,\mathrm{EeV}$, the vacuum term scales as $H_0\propto 1/E$ while the dimension-$d$ LIV term grows as $E^{d-3}$, driving the composition away from $\sim(1:1:1)$. The reference scale is $\mathring{\kappa}^{(d)}_{\alpha\beta}\approx 10^{-23}(\mathrm{GeV}/E)^{d-2}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{4-d}$; for $d=4$ it is $\sim 10^{-33}$ at $100\,\mathrm{TeV}$ and $\sim 10^{-39}$ at $100\,\mathrm{PeV}$. At 95% CL for a moderate flux, the sensitivity is $\sim 10^{-72}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-4}$ for $\mathring{\kappa}^{(8)}_{e\mu}$, $\mathring{\kappa}^{(8)}_{\mu\mu}$, and $\mathring{\kappa}^{(8)}_{\tau\tau}$, while $\mathring{\kappa}^{(8)}_{e\tau}$ is about two orders weaker. A three-flavor analysis improves on Earth-skimming $\nu_\tau$ alone by at most about one order for $d=3$–$8$.
papers.problem: Standard long-baseline averaging drives UHE neutrinos toward a near $(1:1:1)$ flavor composition, but energy-growing LIV operators can produce measurable departures over cosmological propagation baselines.
papers.method: An effective Hamiltonian combines $H_0\propto 1/E$ with an LIV term $\propto E^{d-3}$. Flavor transition probabilities $P_{\alpha\beta}(E,z)$ are obtained by diagonalization and enter $\phi_\beta(E)=\sum_\alpha\int dz\,P_{\alpha\beta}(E,z)\,d\phi_\alpha/dz$. SimProp-v2r4 supplies cosmogenic fluxes for three benchmarks; neutrinos and antineutrinos are combined, and NuFIT best-fit mixing is used. Flavor ratios are compared in windows including $E_{\text{min}}=100\,\mathrm{TeV}$ to $E_{\text{max}}=100\,\mathrm{PeV}$ and $100\,\mathrm{PeV}$ to $10\,\mathrm{EeV}$.
papers.reason: The paper forecasts how ultra-high-energy neutrino flavor ratios constrain isotropic Lorentz-invariance violation, which is relevant to high-energy neutrino observations, but it does not treat compact-object engines, jets, FRBs, or supernova source physics.

papers.title: A self-shadowing black hole accretion disk at sub-Eddington luminosities
papers.result: At outburst peak a vertically extended inner disk shields the outer disk from high-energy radiation near the black hole. The reflection component is approximately 30% of the total X-ray flux in epoch OIR-1, which a standard razor-thin disk cannot produce. An illustrative thickness $H/R\gtrsim 0.05$ suffices to shield the outer disk in systems with orbital periods of tens of hours. The peak is $\sim 0.2L_{\mathrm{Edd}}$; after the luminosity falls to $\lesssim 0.1L_{\mathrm{Edd}}$ and down to $\sim 0.04L_{\mathrm{Edd}}$, strong Balmer and He I lines disappear while weak He II remains, and the ionization is higher at lower luminosity. With $H/R\propto R^{2/7}$, the stated estimate is $H/R\approx 8.9\times 10^{-4}(R/R_{g})^{2/7}$ for $M\approx 8M_{\odot}$ and $L\approx 0.2L_{\mathrm{Edd}}$.
papers.problem: MAXI J0637−430 shows strong low-ionization Balmer and He I lines near peak, but those lines vanish as the luminosity declines, opposite to the expectation that outer-disk irradiation and ionization increase with luminosity. The question is whether a thickened inner disk already self-shadows the outer disk at sub-Eddington luminosity.
papers.method: The outburst is tracked with Swift, NICER, and NuSTAR broadband X-ray spectroscopy and VLT/X-shooter optical/near-IR spectra. The reflection contribution is measured relative to the total flux, and the outer-disk state is diagnosed from Balmer, He I, and He II lines. Ionization is written $\xi=L/(nr^{2})$, and the vertical structure is scaled as $H/R\propto R^{2/7}$.
papers.reason: This stellar-mass black-hole X-ray-binary study is adjacent to compact-object high-energy spectroscopy and photoionization, but it does not address FRBs, supernova engines, relativistic jets, or neutrinos. It is still useful for the sub-Eddington self-shadowing claim, the reflection fraction, and the $H/R$ scale.

papers.title: Revisiting the distance to 4U 1543-475 through X-ray dust-scattering rings
papers.result: Associating the XMM-Newton ring $\theta=9.98\pm0.07$ arcmin with $D_{d}=3.26\pm0.08$ kpc yields $D_{s}=4.6\pm0.2$ kpc, below the usual $7.5$ kpc and consistent with Gaia DR3 $5.0^{+2.0}_{-1.2}$ kpc; the ROSAT ring $\theta=27.2\pm0.3$ arcmin at $D_{d}=1.84\pm0.08$ kpc gives $D_{s}=4\pm1$ kpc. The nearer distance favors an extended horizontal-branch donor ($M_{2}\simeq0.5\,M_{\odot}$) and, for $0.16\le f(M)/M_{\odot}\le0.28$ and $20^{\circ}\le i\le40^{\circ}$, $1.2\lesssim M_{\rm BH}/M_{\odot}\lesssim7.9$. At fixed $9.4\,M_{\odot}$ the 2021 peak Eddington ratio falls from $\sim2.3$ to $\simeq0.87$; rescaling $L/L_{\rm Edd}\propto D^{2}/M_{\rm BH}$ gives $\sim1.0$–$6.8$. $\Gamma$ decreases only slightly and stays highly relativistic relative to the previous bound $\Gamma>4.6$.
papers.problem: The commonly used distance to 4U 1543-475, about $7.5$ kpc with some estimates near $9.1$ kpc, is poorly documented and is larger than the Gaia parallax scale, biasing luminosity, black-hole mass, jet and spin inferences.
papers.method: Archival XMM-Newton EPIC-MOS2 (2002; 0.5–2 keV, $270^{\circ}$–$360^{\circ}$) and ROSAT PSPC (1992; 0.5–2 keV) radial profiles are fit with a constant or power law plus a Lorentzian ring. StarHorse extinction jumps, checked with 3D extinction and CO, fix the dust screens. The source distance is $$D_{s}=\frac{D_{d}}{1-\dfrac{\theta^{2}D_{d}}{2c\Delta t}},$$ using the flare-to-observation delay $\Delta t$.
papers.reason: A geometric dust-scattering distance to the black-hole X-ray binary 4U 1543-475 rescales its luminosity, Eddington ratio, mass and relativistic-jet Lorentz factor, which is useful for compact-object high-energy work but peripheral to FRB/supernova-engine studies.

papers.title: Natal Kicks of Compact Binaries: II. Neutron-star and black-hole systems share similar kick distributions
papers.result: For 66 kinematically constrained systems, neutron-star and black-hole natal kicks are not formally distinguishable (KS $p\simeq0.6$). The joint sample follows $P(\upsilon_{\rm NK}|\alpha,\theta)=\frac{1}{\Gamma(\alpha)\,\theta^{\alpha}}\upsilon_{\rm NK}^{\alpha-1}e^{-\upsilon_{\rm NK}/\theta}$ with $\alpha=1.20^{+0.17}_{-0.26}$ and $\theta=107^{+26}_{-22}\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$, so $\langle\upsilon_{\rm NK}\rangle=\alpha\theta\approx128\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ (also given as $128^{+17}_{-15}\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$) and $\sigma=\theta\sqrt{\alpha}=117\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$. The 68% ranges are $0$–$147\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ for black holes and $0$–$187\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ for neutron stars, while allowed kicks span $\sim0$–$700\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$. The dominant black-hole channel imparts moderate kicks of a few tens to $200\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$, contradicting few-$\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ fallback or neutrino-only expectations; any inverse scaling with black-hole mass is presently insignificant. A fallback-modified Maxwellian with $\sigma=265\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ and the linear $\upsilon_{\rm NK}\propto M_{\rm ej}/M_{\rm CO}$ prescriptions lack sufficient overlap to be compatible.
papers.problem: The conflict is whether fallback and anisotropic-neutrino dilution reduce black-hole kicks to only a few $\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ while neutron stars retain large hydrodynamic kicks, or whether both remnants share a broad $\upsilon_{\rm NK}$ distribution. Observed $\upsilon_{\rm pec}$ is not directly $\upsilon_{\rm NK}$ because companion inertia and orbital angular-momentum changes alter the center-of-mass velocity.
papers.method: Using the Paper I reconstruction and COSMIC population synthesis, each binary receives isotropic kicks from $0$ to $1000\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ in $1\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ steps and 50 directions ($5\times10^{4}$ trials), independent of mechanism and remnant mass. A fixed disk dispersion $\sigma_{\rm dis}=40\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ is subtracted in quadrature from $\upsilon_{\rm pec}$. The empirical distributions are hierarchically fit with dynesty to the Gamma law above, with log-uniform priors $\alpha\in[10^{-2},10^{2}]$ and $\theta\in[1,10^{4}]\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$; post-supernova survival is constrained by the orbital relation involving $\upsilon_{\rm NK}$, $\upsilon_{\rm rel}$, $M_{\rm CO}$, and $M_2$.
papers.reason: The paper quantitatively tests whether supernova fallback, neutrino emission, and explosion asymmetry give neutron stars and black holes different natal kicks, which is relevant to compact-object formation engines, but it does not directly address FRBs, shock breakout, circumstellar interaction, or jets.

papers.title: General Relativistic and Non-Inertial Effects on Magnetic Reconnection Rates
papers.result: In the special-relativistic limit, $\mathcal{R}_{\rm SR}=\mu(1-\mu^2)\sqrt{(1-\mu^2)^3\sigma/[1+(1-\mu^2)^3\sigma]}$ and $\lim\boldsymbol{V}_d|_{\mathfrak{u}}=\mathcal{R}_{\rm SR}/(1+\mu^2)$. The corrected symmetric rate is $\mathcal{R}=\mu A\boldsymbol{V}^{L}_{\mathfrak{o}}$, with $(\boldsymbol{V}^{L}_{\mathfrak{o}})^2/[1-(\boldsymbol{V}^{L}_{\mathfrak{o}})^2]=(1-\mu^2)A^2\sigma$ and an anticipated $\mathcal{R}\sim 0.1V_A$. Light has coordinate speed $ds/dt=\pm|\vec{\tau}|$, so $\mathcal{C}^{\pm}=1\pm\frac{1}{2}\boldsymbol{a}_y w_y^{\pm}-\frac{1}{6}(S_{yy}-\boldsymbol{a}_y^2)(w_y^{\pm})^2+\mathcal{O}((w_y^{\pm})^3)$. For Schwarzschild accretion, $\bar{Q}=\bar{S}+\bar{\mathcal{K}}$ and curvature scales as $\kappa\equiv r_s/r^3$; all gravitational contributions enhance reconnection together only near the orientation where $\bar{S}$ and $\bar{\mathcal{K}}$ are most negative. Outside a very narrow region just outside the horizon, an inertial rate is adequate. The stated amplitude parameter is $\bar{\kappa}\equiv r_s\Delta y^2/r^3$.
papers.problem: Standard reconnection theory assumes an inertial frame in flat spacetime, while curved-spacetime extensions can mix real gravitational effects with coordinate artifacts. The problem is to define a gauge-invariant rate and isolate leading non-inertial and curvature corrections near a compact source.
papers.method: The rate is built from the Faraday flux one-form $\mathrm{d}\psi\equiv F\cdot\vec{\zeta}$, with steady-state $E_r=\partial_t\psi/(|\vec{\zeta}||\vec{\tau}|)$ and drift $\boldsymbol{V}_d=E_r/|\vec{\boldsymbol{B}}_r|$. Liu et al. mesoscale theory is expanded in Fermi coordinates through acceleration, tidal tensor $\mathbb{S}$, geodesic-deviation tensor $\mathbb{Q}$, and Gaussian curvature $\mathcal{K}$; general-relativistic corrections are omitted inside the diffusion region. The application uses $c=1$ Lorentz–Heaviside electrodynamics for zero-angular-momentum accretion in a static spherical metric, with near-zone Ricci flatness $\mathrm{Ric}_{yy}|_{\mathtt{x}}=S_{yy}+\mathcal{K}-Q_{yy}=0$.
papers.reason: The paper gives a gauge-invariant leading-order correction to magnetic reconnection in zero-angular-momentum accretion plasma around a spherical compact object, relevant to dissipation near compact objects, but it does not treat FRBs, jet radiation, supernovae, or neutrinos.

papers.title: A faint thermonuclear X-ray burst from SAX~J1808.4--3658 observed with NICER: possible evidence for burst-driven changes in the inner disk structure
papers.result: Peak flux reaches ~5% of Eddington limit; post-burst tail stabilizes at 0.46 keV with flux 14% above pre-burst; visible surface area increases by factor of ~4 at peak and remains ~1.6 times higher afterward; $f_a \propto F_{\rm bb}^{1/2}$ (direct) steepens to nearly linear after occultation correction; cooling index $\alpha=-1.67\pm0.11$; recovery timescale consistent with viscous refilling at $R\sim70$–100 km.
papers.problem: Whether faint (sub-Eddington) thermonuclear X-ray bursts can alter the inner accretion geometry and neutron-star visibility in SAX J1808.4–3658.
papers.method: NICER data reduction with nicerl2/nicerl3 and 3C50 background; time-resolved spectroscopy using tbabs*(bbodyrad+thcomp*diskbb) and $f_a$ model; comparison of pre-/post-burst persistent emission and burst-tail cooling; timing analysis of 0.5–10 keV light curves.
papers.reason: Reports NICER observations of a faint thermonuclear burst from the accreting millisecond pulsar SAX J1808.4–3658 showing burst-driven changes to inner-disk geometry and visible neutron-star area, relevant to compact-object high-energy observations.

papers.title: Energetic Particle Confinement In Black Hole Accretion Disks
papers.result: Passive particles in ADAF funnels reach acceleration factors up to $10^{2}$ through turbulent scattering; the jet/funnel sheath ($\sigma\approx 1$) is the dominant energization site and has the largest escape time $\tau_{\rm esc}$. Particles already at $\Gamma\approx 10^{8}$ can gain a further factor $\times 100$ by $\nabla B$ reflection along the jet. Extended MAD escape satisfies $\langle\tau_{\rm esc}\rangle>1.2\times 10^{3}\,t_g$, above a naive $\sim 870\,r_g/c$ estimate, while infall in $\mathbb{M}9$ can exceed free streaming by more than ten and high-energy escape is near free streaming. The uniform diffusivity $\nu=[(\Delta R)^{2}+(\Delta z)^{2}]/(2\eta\tau_{\rm trap})$ ($\eta=4$) does not describe the transport. Particles below the turbulent energy, or with a Larmor radius comparable to magnetic structures, gain energy on average, whereas higher-energy particles lose energy; late single-energy subsets favor $\xi\approx 1.2$, with no single index fitting all times.
papers.problem: The core question is how SANE and MAD accretion states change confinement, escape, and acceleration of energetic charged particles in a black-hole ADAF, motivated by the IceCube $(1-15)$ TeV neutrino excess toward NGC 1068 and the inference that a corona at $r\lesssim 30\,r_g$ is the more likely source.
papers.method: AthenaK evolves ideal GRMHD ADAFs in Cartesian Kerr–Schild coordinates with a $3+1$ split, starting from Fishbone–Moncrief tori plus weak poloidal flux and MRI-driven turbulence, in MAD and high-spin SANE states. Fully passive tracers are then integrated once with a $3+1$ geodesic pusher plus grid electromagnetic fields, using implicit midpoint and Newton–Raphson iteration at residual tolerance $10^{-16}$. Diagnostics use $\Gamma=\sqrt{1+\gamma^{ij}u_i u_j}$ and $\Gamma=\alpha u^{0}$, $\omega_L=\alpha eB/(2\pi\Gamma m)\,t_g^{-1}$, $\tau^{-1}_{\rm acc}=(\Delta\Gamma/\Gamma)\tau_{\rm trap}^{-1}$, and $\nu=[(\Delta R)^{2}+(\Delta z)^{2}]/(2\eta\tau_{\rm trap})$; phase-space evolution is compared with a diffusion–advection model.
papers.reason: The paper is relevant to relativistic jet sheaths and compact-object neutrino emission, especially the NGC 1068 corona, but it is an incremental GRMHD tracer study of steady SMBH ADAFs rather than a direct FRB, supernova-engine, or CSM-shock result.

papers.title: Search for gravitational wave coincident neutrinos in DEAP-3600
papers.result: No statistically significant neutrino excess is found for seven neutron-star-containing mergers. All seven negative-log-likelihood values fall below their 90% CL critical values $\alpha$, so the on-time data are consistent with background only. Region R1 counts agree within $2\sigma$; the only out-of-region count is one event in R2 for GW190426_152155, against $(0.47^{+0.69}_{-0.47})$ expected ($p=0.376$). For the monoenergetic model, the GW170817 electron-neutrino fluence limits are $6.8\times10^{12}\,\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$ at 10 MeV and $1.8\times10^{10}\,\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$ at 100 MeV, using $\Phi_{\rm limit}(E_i)=N_{\rm limit}(E_i)/[n_t\varepsilon(E_i)\phi(E_i)\sigma(E_i)]$.
papers.problem: Neutron-star-containing compact mergers are expected to emit neutrinos, but no gravitational-wave-coincident neutrinos have been detected; the question is whether DEAP-3600 sees $\nu_e$ within a 1000 s window of LVK merger alerts.
papers.method: DEAP-3600 searches $(3269\pm24)\,\mathrm{kg}$ of liquid argon for charged-current $\nu_e$ absorption, using a total 1000 s coincidence window and LVK sidebands for background. Because the merger spectrum is unknown, flat, $E^{-2}$, supernova-like, and monoenergetic hypotheses are tested. The prompt fraction is $F_{\rm prompt}=\sum_{t=-28\,\mathrm{ns}}^{150\,\mathrm{ns}}\mathrm{PE}(t)/\sum_{t=-28\,\mathrm{ns}}^{10\,\mu\mathrm{s}}\mathrm{PE}(t)$, with $0.1<F_{\rm prompt}<0.35$ and $\mathrm{PE}>16885$ ($\sim2.4\,\mathrm{MeV}$). Bound final states use $E_{\nu}=E_{\rm vis}+1.5\,\mathrm{MeV}$; limits use Feldman–Cousins counts and Poisson NLL pseudo-experiments.
papers.reason: This is a null but quantitative electron-neutrino coincidence search for LVK compact-object mergers, directly relevant to neutrinos from compact remnants, though it does not address FRB, supernova-engine, shock, or jet physics.

papers.title: Frequency-dependent time delays in Sgr A* from a broadband VLA observation
papers.result: One broad brightening is present across $\sim 13$–$36\,\mathrm{GHz}$, with the maximum later at lower frequency. Peak-time and LCCF slopes agree at $\mathcal{S}\sim 40\,\mathrm{min\,cm^{-1}}$: excluding the reference, $\mathcal{S}_{\rm peak}=41.2\pm 10.2\,\mathrm{min\,cm^{-1}}$ and $\mathcal{S}_{\rm LCCF}=40.4\pm 5.8\,\mathrm{min\,cm^{-1}}$. Checks give $\mathcal{S}_{\rm peak}=46.7\pm 8.0$, $42.3\pm 10.8$, and $40.9\pm 10.6\,\mathrm{min\,cm^{-1}}$. The Ka-to-lowest-Ku peak lag is $81.1\pm 12.5\,\mathrm{min}$, while the lowest Ku LCCF lag is $58.4\pm 12.1\,\mathrm{min}$. These match earlier slopes $42\pm 14$ and $40.3\pm 2.0\,\mathrm{min\,cm^{-1}}$ and are associated with outward motion at $\gamma\beta\sim 0.5$–$1.2$, without uniquely separating a jet from adiabatic synchrotron expansion.
papers.problem: Sgr A* radio variations usually lead at higher frequency, but it is unresolved whether the delay comes from a jet, an expanding plasma, or magnetic-flux eruption and whether the positive delay–wavelength trend recurs.
papers.method: A $\sim 6\,\mathrm{h}$ VLA A-configuration track on 2022 May 28 covers Ku/K/Ka (effective $\sim 13$–$36\,\mathrm{GHz}$). Stokes $I$ light curves are taken from visibility real parts on baselines $>150\,\mathrm{k}\lambda$, median-normalized, $1\,\mathrm{min}$ binned, and smoothed with a FWHM $7\,\mathrm{min}$ Gaussian; lags use peak times and an LCCF on $100$–$290\,\mathrm{min}$ with $50\%$ Monte Carlo errors. The minispiral test fits $V(t)=S_1(t)V^{\rm ext}+S_2(t)V^{\rm compact}$ on $<150\,\mathrm{k}\lambda$. Because $S_1(t)$ varies by $\sim 30$–$50\%$ with no systematic trend, amplitudes rely on 3C 286 and phase self-calibration. The extended-emission index is $S_\nu\propto\nu^\alpha$.
papers.reason: This VLA study quantifies a recurring frequency-dependent radio lag in Sgr A* and links it to a mildly relativistic outflow, which is relevant to compact-object jet timing but is outside the group's core FRB, supernova-engine, and dispersion-measure problems.

papers.title: Rebrightening in the Radio: Secondary Flares from Tidal Disruption Events AT2019ehz and AT2019eve
papers.result: AT2019ehz ($z=0.074$) rebrightens at 1545 d, and its secondary flare is attributed to a second outflow launched near $1000$ d (linear $R_{\rm eq}$ extrapolation $1071^{+62}_{-79}$ d), with mean $\bar{\beta}=v/c$ rising from $0.003$ to $0.033$. AT2019eve ($z=0.081$) rebrightens at 1594 d with $L\sim6.7\times10^{38}$–$1\times10^{39}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$, about $2$–$3\times$ the earlier $3.6\times10^{38}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$, while $\nu_p$ rises from $1.6$ to $2.8\,\mathrm{GHz}$ at $F_{\nu,p}\sim1.0\,\mathrm{mJy}$. Its $R_{\rm eq}$ appears to fall by ${\sim}8\times10^{16}\,\mathrm{cm}$ over ${\sim}1000$ d; $\beta\lesssim0.06$ does not reach the off-axis-jet value $\beta_{\rm eq,N}=0.44$. Under a prompt launch, $E\sim7\times10^{48}\,\mathrm{erg}$ while $v$ declines from $0.06c$ to $0.02c$. Sample densities scale from $(R/R_s)^{-1}$ to $(R/R_s)^{-2}$; AT2019ehz is on average $\propto R^{-2}$ and AT2019eve $\propto R^{-1}$.
papers.problem: The paper asks what produces secondary radio flares $\approx1550$–$1600$ d after optical TDE discovery—variable CSM, a decelerating off-axis jet, a delayed accretion-driven outflow, or a repeating partial TDE—especially when AT2019eve's synchrotron peak frequency rises instead of falling.
papers.method:
New VLA ${\sim}1$–$18\,\mathrm{GHz}$ data are imaged in CASA, and per-band rises are fit by power laws with index $\alpha$. SEDs use a non-relativistic synchrotron Granot & Sari form $F_{
