papers.reason: The two late TDE radio rebrightenings give quantitative outflow, jet, and circumstellar-density constraints relevant to relativistic outflows and CSM interaction, but they are incremental relative to the group's core FRB, supernova-engine, and neutrino focus.

papers.title: Self-Regulated Cosmic-Ray Electron Acceleration in High-Mach-Number MHD-PIC Shocks
papers.result: Across supplied CRe mass fractions, the upstream magnetic pressure saturates at a common level $\langle B^{2}\rangle/B_{0}^{2}\approx 12$; increasing $\eta$ mainly shortens the time to saturation. Despite $r_{\rm tot}\simeq 5$, for which $q_p=3r/(r-1)=3.75$, the high-energy spectrum stays near the test-particle form $4\pi f(p)p^{4}=\mathrm{const}$ ($q_p=4$) rather than forming a concave NLDSA spectrum. The resolved-tail effective pressure converges to $P_{\rm CR}^{\rm eff}\sim 0.3\rho_0 v_0^2$ for $p/p_0\simeq 100$–$1000$, while low-momentum normalizations retain a strong $\eta$ dependence.
papers.problem: Efficient DSA is predicted to build a smooth CR-pressure precursor that hardens the spectrum above the strong-shock test-particle slope $f(p)\propto p^{-4}$, yet observations favor $4\pi f(p)p^{4}=\mathrm{const}$ or steeper spectra.
papers.method: Non-relativistic quasi-parallel shocks with $M_{\rm A}=M_s=50$ are evolved in Athena MHD-PIC: the thermal plasma is ideal MHD, CRe are macroparticles with $\bm{\mathcal{E}}=-({\bm v}_g\times{\bm B})/c$ and feedback $-{\bm F}_{\rm CR}$, and the control parameter is the supplied CRe mass fraction $\eta$ rather than a fixed injection efficiency. Self-regulation is measured through saturation of the electron-driven Bell mode and the resulting SLAMS-dominated upstream.
papers.reason: This MHD-PIC study of self-regulated cosmic-ray electron DSA at a high-Mach quasi-parallel shock is useful for SNR shock spectra and magnetic amplification, but it is not directly about FRBs, central engines, shock breakout, jets, or neutrinos.

papers.title: Hump around 30 keV in Suzaku spectra of Aquila X-1 -- Possible evidence of strong rapid-proton capture process --
papers.result: The hard-state hump is fit by a radiative-recombination redge with $E_{\rm K}=27\pm 1$ keV and $kT_{\rm e}=11^{+10}_{-5}$ keV; after gravitational redshift this corresponds to $Z\approx 48$–49. The weighted equivalent width is $\overline{\rm EW}=5.6\pm 1.9$ keV. Matching the flux requires $n_{\rm x}n_{\rm e}V\sim 3\times 10^{53}\,{\rm cm^{-3}}$ and $n_{\rm x}/n_{\rm H}\gtrsim 8\times 10^{-4}$, or $X_{\rm x}\gtrsim 0.06(A_{\rm x}/100)(X_{\rm H}/0.73)$, roughly $\sim 10^{7}$ times the solar Cd abundance. One-zone rp-process models favor stable ${}^{106}{\rm Cd}$, with a mass fraction up to 38% and survival for $\gtrsim 10$ days; convective mixing gives $\tau\equiv\Delta M_0/\dot{M}\sim 10^{7}\,{\rm s}$.
papers.problem: The issue is whether the approximately 30 keV hard-state hump in Aql X-1 is a radiative-recombination quasi-continuum from highly ionized Cd or In produced by the rp-process, despite the observed strength greatly exceeding that expected for solar Cd abundance.
papers.method: Suzaku spectra are modeled with tbabs ($N_{\rm H}=0.36\times 10^{22}\,{\rm cm^{-2}}$), a blackbody, CompPS thermal Comptonization, an Fe K line, and a redge; Gaussian equivalent widths are compared with an expected K$\alpha$ cascade near $0.75E_{\rm K}$. Atmospheric constraints use $H=kT_{\rm e}/(m_{\rm i}g)$ and $\Phi_{\rm rec}=n_{\rm x}n_{\rm e}V\int_{E_{\rm K}}^{\infty}S(E)dE$. One-zone bursts use JINA Reaclib, while post-burst retention is tested with Taylor–Spruit mixing and dilution.
papers.reason: This is a quantitative hard-state neutron-star X-ray study linking a 30 keV Suzaku feature in Aql X-1 to rp-process ashes, so it is relevant to compact-object high-energy observations, but it does not address FRBs, supernova engines, jets, neutrinos, shocks, or dispersion measure.

papers.title: 3D radiative transfer of K-series lines of He-like ions with SKIRT
papers.result: For photoionized Fe at $n=10^{10}\,\mathrm{cm}^{-3}$ and $\xi=10^{3.1}$, resonance scattering suppresses the cores and boosts the wings of He-like $w$ and $y$ for $N_{\mathrm{H}}\gtrsim10^{22}$ and $\gtrsim10^{23}\,\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$, respectively, while $x$ and $z$ stay nearly unchanged. $I/N_{\mathrm{H}}$ declines with column for $w,y$ and is nearly constant for $x,z$; Fe XXV $w,y$ are RS-dominated and form P Cygni profiles in outflow, whereas $x,z$ are mainly RR/II and do not. The $w$ emissivity and Fe$^{+24}$ fraction peak at $\log\xi\simeq 3.3$. A polarized-beam test gives $|Q_{\mathrm{sca}}|/I_{\mathrm{sca}}\simeq 1$ for dipole $w,y$ over most angles, with partial depolarization near $\theta=90^{\circ}$.
papers.problem: XRISM resolves He-like K-line profiles, including P Cygni profiles, in photoionized plasma around compact objects, but standard 1D radiative transfer uses the escape-probability approximation and does not treat frequency redistribution by resonance scattering explicitly.
papers.method: SKIRT performs 3D Monte Carlo transfer of He-like K lines ($Z=2$–$30$, $n\to 1$ up to $n=10$) with resonance scattering, radiative recombination, and Li-like inner-shell ionization. The ionization parameter is $\xi\equiv L_{\mathrm{X}}/(n_{\mathrm{H}}r^{2})$, and excited-level populations obey $\dot{\bm{N}}=\bm{\Gamma}\bm{N}+\bm{S}=\bm{0}$ with H-like, He-like, and Li-like densities and $T_{e}$ prescribed externally. Coherent E1 scattering uses $\bm{M}(\theta)=E_1\bm{M}^{(m)}+E_2\bm{M}^{(d)}$ with $E_1+E_2=1$; verification uses $10^{10}$ packets on a Cloudy-structured Fe shell.
papers.reason: This is a 3D Monte Carlo radiative-transfer method for He-like K-series lines in photoionized gas around compact objects, including P Cygni profiles seen by XRISM, so it is useful for photoionization and compact-object high-energy spectroscopy but is not a direct FRB, supernova-engine, jet, or neutrino result.

papers.title: EP250226a: A fast X-ray transient associated with GRB 250226A and its multiwavelength afterglow properties
papers.result: EP250226a/GRB 250226A is at $z=3.314$ with $E_{\mathrm{iso}}\simeq 7.32\times 10^{53}\,\mathrm{erg}$. The X-ray and optical afterglow is nearly achromatic, with no strong rising phase, plateau, or jet break. A uniform-ISM top-hat forward shock is preferred over a wind; the reported fit gives $E_{\mathrm{k,iso}}\simeq 4.07\times 10^{55}\,\mathrm{erg}$, $\eta_{\gamma}\simeq 1.77\%$, and $\log\epsilon_{\mathrm{B,FS}}\simeq -6.52$, so most jet energy remains kinetic. The wind closure estimate $p(\alpha_{\mathrm{o}})\simeq 1.69$ conflicts with $p>2$.
papers.problem: The paper tests whether EP250226a is a classical long/Type II GRB associated with GRB 250226A and whether its multiwavelength afterglow arises in a uniform ISM or a wind-like circumburst medium.
papers.method: High-energy spectra are fit with absorbed power-law and cutoff power-law models, while the afterglow is tested with closure relations $F_\nu\propto\nu^{-\beta}$ and $p(\alpha)$. The preferred physical model is a Bayesian top-hat forward-shock fit in a uniform ISM; INTEGRAL sees one pulse with $T_{90}=33\pm 1\,\mathrm{s}$ above 80 keV.
papers.reason: This is a high-redshift Einstein Probe fast X-ray transient coincident with a classical long GRB, with quantitative afterglow constraints on jet energy, radiative efficiency, and ISM versus wind circumburst medium.

papers.title: Polarized transport in a Thomson slab: Stokes recursion, asymptotic eigenmodes, and Comptonization applications
papers.result: In finite Thomson slabs, polarized transport at high scattering orders is dominated by a unique self-adjoint spatial eigenmode with leading eigenvalue $\lambda_0$, yielding an asymptotic escape probability ratio $\lim_{n\to\infty} P_n^\pm / P_{n-1}^\pm = \lambda_0$. In the optically thin limit ($\tau \ll 1$), the leading eigenvalue scales as $\lambda_0 = \frac{3\tau}{4}\left[\ln(1/\tau) + \frac{3}{4} - \gamma_{\rm E} + \mathcal{O}(1/\ln(1/\tau))\right]$ with asymptotic escape polarization approaching $\Pi_\infty^\pm \to -1$. In the optically thick limit ($\tau \gg 1$), transport splits into a diffusion branch $\lambda_{\rm D}(k) = 1 - k^2/3 + \mathcal{O}(k^4)$ and a rapidly suppressed polarization branch $\lambda_{\rm P}(k) = 7/10 - (29/210)k^2 + \mathcal{O}(k^4)$, leading to $\lambda_0 = 1 - k_1^2/3 + \mathcal{O}(k_1^4)$ with wavenumber $k_1 \simeq \pi / (\tau + 2z_0)$ and Milne extrapolation length $z_0 \simeq 0.7121$. The mean scattering order satisfies $\langle N\rangle_{\rm int}^{\rm pol} \simeq \frac{\tau^2}{4} + \frac{3}{2}z_0 \tau$. Application to IXPE/NuSTAR/NICER spectro-polarimetry of 4U 1624–49 constrains electron temperature $kT_{\rm e} \simeq 2.65\text{ keV}$, optical depth $\tau = 13.10^{+1.14}_{-0.98}$, and inclination $i = 81.6^{\circ+2.8}_{-5.6}$, explaining the observed $\sim 3.2\%$ polarization via a slab corona geometry.
papers.problem: Accurately modeling line-polarized radiation transport, polarization feedback on angular redistribution, escape statistics, and energy-resolved Stokes spectra in finite-optical-depth Thomson scattering coronae around compact objects.
papers.method: Formulation of an exact scattering-order-resolved Stokes recursion $\bm{\Psi}_{n+1}(t',\mu') = \int_0^\tau {\rm d}t \int_{-1}^1 {\rm d}\mu\, \textbf{P}(\mu',\mu) G(t',t;\mu) \bm{\Psi}_n(t,\mu)$ via a two-coefficient angular closure $(a_n(t), b_n(t))$; spectral decomposition of the self-adjoint integral operator $\textbf{K}_{\rm pol}$ across thin (Galerkin approximation) and thick (half-space Milne matching) limits; synthesis of energy-resolved spectra using the Jones angle-averaged thermal Compton redistribution kernel $\mathcal{R}_{\rm J}$; and cross-validation via an independent polarized Monte Carlo radiative transfer (MCRT) code.
papers.reason: The paper develops a rigorous scattering-order Stokes recursion and asymptotic eigenmode formalism for polarized transport in Thomson slabs, providing essential theoretical tools to model polarized Comptonization in compact object accretion coronae such as the neutron star X-ray binary 4U 1624–49 observed by IXPE.

papers.title: Self-Organizing Maps for the Exploration and Classification of X-Ray Sources in the Chandra Source Catalog
papers.result: The SOM successfully segregates distinct high-energy radiation regimes: neoAGNs populate the central region with hard spectra and multi-component emission; neoYSOs map to the lower boundary with $kT \in [0.5, 1.5]\ \mathrm{keV}$ and $\Gamma \in [0, 3]$; Binaries cluster in the upper-right with hard spectra ($kT \in [1, 5]\ \mathrm{keV}$) and high variability. In PartOfG sources, it isolates M87 relativistic jet knots (accounting for $\sim 76\%$ of detections at neuron $(x=36, y=9)$) dominated by non-thermal synchrotron emission. SOMClassifier attains Macro-$F_1 = 0.654$ and Micro-$F_1 = 0.737$, classifying $6{,}225$ of $11{,}712$ unlabeled detections ($53\%$ coverage).
papers.problem: Simple absorbed blackbody ($kT$) and absorbed power-law ($F_E \propto E^{-\nu}$) spectral models yield $\chi_\nu^2 \gg 1$ for high-$\mathrm{S/N}$ Chandra detections, failing to capture diverse physical emission mechanisms across compact binaries, AGNs, and relativistic jet knots in high-dimensional parameter spaces.
papers.method: Constructs an 11-dimensional feature space from distance-independent hardness ratios $\mathrm{HR}_{xy} = \frac{F(x)-F(y)}{F(x)+F(y)}$, spectral fit parameters ($kT$, $\Gamma$), and multi-band variability metrics ($\mathrm{var\_ratio} = \sigma_{\mathrm{var}} / \mu_{\mathrm{var}}$, $\mathrm{var\_prob}$). Trains a $40 \times 40$ hexagonal SOM using weight update $W(t+1) = W(t) + \theta(t)\cdot\alpha(t)\cdot(V - W(t))$ reaching quantization error $E_q = 0.164$ and topographic error $E_t = 0.037$, and develops an RBF-kernel neighborhood classifier with class weights $w_k = [c / (\mathrm{class\_counts}_k + \varepsilon)]^\gamma$ ($\gamma = 0.7$, $\sigma_f = 0.05$).
papers.reason: This work establishes a Self-Organizing Map (SOM) pipeline to classify and inspect emission mechanisms across $36{,}904$ Chandra ACIS X-ray detections, providing useful methodology for compact object high-energy source classification and jet knot diagnostics.

papers.title: The $w$-mode instability of strangeon ergostars and its impact on energy extraction
papers.result: Along maximum-energy-extraction paths across all 12 Lennard-Jones strangeon EOS models (A–L), both the $l=m=2$ axial-led and polar-led $w$-modes remain strictly damped with $\mathrm{Im}(\sigma) > 0$. The stability margin $\eta_{\Omega} = \Omega_1 / \Omega_{\rm crit} < 1$ demonstrates that even for the most weakly damped configuration (Model H), the critical rotation rate exceeds the extraction-path rate by $\approx 8\%$ (i.e. $\Omega_{\rm crit} \approx 1.08\,\Omega_1$), confirming that the rotational energy reservoir of $\sim 0.01\,M_\odot c^2 \sim 10^{52}\,\mathrm{erg}$ is preserved against gravitational radiation.
papers.problem: Whether non-axisymmetric $w$-mode instability in rapidly rotating strangeon ergostars operates as a competitive dissipation channel that siphons rotational energy into gravitational waves instead of powering relativistic jets in short gamma-ray bursts.
papers.method: Linearized Einstein-fluid perturbation theory in the Hilbert gauge $\nabla^a \psi_{ab} = 0$, discretized into a quadratic matrix eigenvalue problem $(\mathbf{A}_0 + \sigma\mathbf{A}_1 + \sigma^2\mathbf{A}_2)\boldsymbol{x} = 0$ via Chebyshev pseudo-spectral expansion, combined with exterior complex scaling (ECS) for outgoing waves and explicit surface jump matching $\left.(\partial_r \psi_{ab}^{\rm in} - \partial_r \psi_{ab}^{\rm out})\right|_\Sigma = \frac{16\pi \rho_{\rm sur} \xi}{W_\Sigma} u_a u_b$.
papers.reason: Investigates whether non-axisymmetric $w$-mode instabilities deplete the rotational energy reservoir of strangeon ergostars as alternative sGRB central engines, finding them dynamically stable along maximum-energy-extraction paths.

papers.title: A Dark-Sector Mass Flip-Flop Mechanism for the ANITA-IV Events
papers.result: Four near-horizon ANITA-IV upward showers are attributed to atmospheric $N_2\to N_1 Z'$ rather than $\nu_\tau$. Matter-induced ordering reversal opens underground $N_1\to N_2 Z'$ while kinematics $|M_1(h)-M_2|\le M_{Z'}$ blocks decays at IceCube. For $M_{Z'}=1\,\mathrm{GeV}$ and $y_1=-1$, BP1 and BP2 give $(h_-,h_+)\simeq(-1.15,14.77)\,\mathrm{km}$ and $(-0.96,9.95)\,\mathrm{km}$. At $g_{12}=10^{-5}$, $\int\mathcal{A}\,d\mathcal{H}=1.7\,\mathrm{km}^{2}\,\mathrm{sr}$ (BP1) and $5.4\,\mathrm{km}^{2}\,\mathrm{sr}$ (BP2); at $E_1=20\,\mathrm{EeV}$, increasing $g_{12}$ to $10^{-4}$ raises the BP1 peak from $10$ to $26\,\mathrm{km}^{2}$. The lab lengths scale as $\ell_i\simeq E_i/[M_i\Gamma_{ij}]$ and $\ell_{Z'}\propto E_{Z'}g_B^{-2}$; for $g_B=10^{-3}$, $E_{Z'}=1\,\mathrm{EeV}$ and $M_{Z'}\gtrsim 0.7\,\mathrm{GeV}$, $\ell_{Z'}<0.1\,\mathrm{km}$. Normalized to four ANITA-IV events, the associated IceCube signal is $\ll 1$, while PUEO's first flight expects about 3 events. The standard $\nu_\tau$ joint tension exceeds $7\sigma$, and a rare-transient case still exceeds $5\sigma$.
papers.problem: ANITA-IV reports four upward-going, non-inverted, cosmic-ray-like air showers just below the horizon, nominally consistent with ultra-high-energy $\nu_\tau$, but IceCube sees no corresponding events, creating a $>7\sigma$ tension ($>5\sigma$ even for rare transients).
papers.method: Two dark fermions $N_1,N_2$, an ultralight scalar $\phi$, and a GeV-scale $Z'$ undergo a density-dependent mass flip-flop, $M_1(\mathbf{x})=M_1^{(0)}+\delta M_1(\mathbf{x})$. For $M_i>M_j+M_{Z'}$, the rest-frame width is $\Gamma_{ij}$ with $\lambda(a,b,c)=a^2+b^2+c^2-2ab-2ac-2bc$; the lab length is $\ell_i(s,E_i)\simeq E_i/[M_i(s)\Gamma_{ij}(s)]$, and survival follows an exponential integral of $\ell_i^{-1}$. In the unpolarized ultrarelativistic limit, $z\equiv E_{Z'}/E_i$ is uniform on $(z_-,z_+)$. ANITA-IV effective area is computed semi-analytically along $N_1\to N_2\to\mathrm{EAS}$ using position-dependent decay and energy transport, matched to the Standard Model $\nu_\tau$ visible-shower response.
papers.reason: The paper targets the ANITA-IV upward air-shower versus IceCube null ultra-high-energy neutrino tension, so it is relevant to high-energy neutrino observations, but its dark-sector mass flip-flop is peripheral to FRB, supernova-engine, and jet studies.

papers.title: On the MeV Nuclear De-excitation Line Emission from the Vela Supernova Remnant Region
papers.result: Vela dominates the predicted line flux among the three SNRs, particularly for soft injected proton spectra. Distinct lines are at $1.63\,\mathrm{MeV}$ (mainly $^{20}\mathrm{Ne}$), $4.44\,\mathrm{MeV}$ (mainly $^{12}\mathrm{C}$), and $6.13\,\mathrm{MeV}$ (mainly $^{16}\mathrm{O}$), with integrated fluxes about $1.3\times10^{-10}$–$1.2\times10^{-6}$, $3.2\times10^{-10}$–$5.6\times10^{-7}$, and $1.6\times10^{-10}$–$2.6\times10^{-7}\,\mathrm{ph\,cm^{-2}\,s^{-1}}$. For $\alpha=4.0$, the Vela $4.44$ and $6.13\,\mathrm{MeV}$ FWHMs are about $0.10$ and $0.12\,\mathrm{MeV}$; the $1.63$ and $4.44\,\mathrm{MeV}$ lines are below the COSI two-year narrow-line point-source sensitivity.
papers.problem: Whether low-energy cosmic rays below the pion-production threshold of about $280\,\mathrm{MeV}$ in Vela, Vela Jr., and Puppis A can generate MeV nuclear de-excitation lines above the Galactic diffuse MeV continuum and local inverse-Compton continuum.
papers.method: Direct and inverse proton and $\alpha$-particle reactions are calculated with TALYS 2.2, discarding ENSDF-unsupported lines. The proton spectrum is $dN/dE=A(E/1\,\mathrm{GeV})^{-\alpha}\exp(-E/E_{\rm cut})$, using $\alpha=3.0$ and $4.0$ for Vela and $\alpha=1.8$ plus $2.0,2.3,2.6$ for the other SNRs. Vela is also fit with $\alpha_1=2.2$, $E_{\rm b}$ limited to $5$–$10\,\mathrm{GeV}$, and $\alpha_2\simeq2.74$, normalized to $W_p=4\times10^{49}\,\mathrm{erg}$. Abundances follow $(X/X_{\odot})_{\rm total}=\sum_i(X/X_{\odot})_i N_{{\rm H},i}/\sum_i N_{{\rm H},i}$ with $N_{{\rm H},i}\approx\sqrt{EM_i V_i}$; the diffuse spectrum is $I(E)=C_0(E/1\,\mathrm{MeV})^{\alpha}$.
papers.reason: The work predicts MeV nuclear de-excitation lines from low-energy cosmic rays in the Vela SNR complex and does not substantially address FRB/PRS environments, supernova central engines, shock breakout or CSM-powered emission, jets, neutrinos, or compact-object engine physics.
